In a large saucepan, heat oil over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir 1 minute. Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, water, sugar and salt; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; simmer, uncovered, 1 to 1-1/2 hours or until flavors are blended, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, for gnocchi, in a large bowl, mix ricotta cheese, eggs, Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, salt and pepper until blended. Stir in enough flour to form a soft dough that holds its shape.
In a Dutch oven, bring 4 quarts water to a boil. Divide dough into eight portions. Roll each into a ½-in.-thick rope; cut crosswise into ¾-in. pieces.
Cook gnocchi in batches in boiling water 2-3 minutes or until they float; remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well. Add gnocchi to sauce; gently stir in mozzarella cheese. If desired, sprinkle with basil.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
4 cups grape tomatoes, chopped
1 cup shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese
¾ cup water-packed artichoke hearts, rinsed, drained and chopped
3  green onions, chopped
3 tbsp. pine nuts, toasted
¼ cup olive oil
3 tbsp. red wine vinegar
3  garlic cloves, minced
¾ tsp. pepper
¼ tsp. salt
1  French bread baguette (10½ ounces), cut into  ¼-inch slices
recipes.Procedure:
Preheat oven to 425°. In a large bowl, combine tomatoes, cheese, artichokes, green onions and pine nuts. Whisk the oil, vinegar, garlic, pepper and salt; pour over tomato mixture and toss to coat.
Place bread on ungreased baking sheets. Bake 4-5 minutes on each side or until golden brown. Top with tomato mixture.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tsp. olive oil
2  garlic cloves, minced
1 can (14½ ounces) no-salt-added diced tomatoes, undrained
3 cans (14½ ounces each) vegetable broth
2 tsp. Italian seasoning
1  package (9 ounces) refrigerated cheese tortellini
4 cups fresh baby spinach
Shredded Parmesan cheese and freshly ground pepper
recipes.Procedure:
In a large saucepan, heat oil over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir 1 minute. Stir in tomatoes, broth and Italian seasoning; bring to a boil. Add tortellini; bring to a gentle boil. Cook, uncovered, just until tortellini are tender, 7-9 minutes.
Stir in spinach. Sprinkle servings with cheese and pepper.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
1  broiler/fryer chicken (3½ to 4 pounds), cut up
¼ cup all-purpose flour
Salt and pepper to taste
2 tbsp. olive oil
2 tbsp. butter
1  large onion, chopped
2  celery ribs, sliced
1  large green pepper, cut into strips
½ lb. sliced fresh mushrooms
1 can (28 ounces) tomatoes, cut up and juice reserved
1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce
1 can (6 ounces) tomato paste
1 cup dry red wine or water
1 tsp. dried thyme
1 tsp. dried rosemary, crushed
1 tsp. dried oregano
1 tsp. dried basil
3  garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp. sugar
Hot cooked pasta
Grated Parmesan cheese
recipes.Procedure:
Dust chicken with flour. Season with salt and pepper. In a large skillet, brown chicken on all sides in oil and butter over medium-high heat. Remove chicken to platter. 
In the same skillet, cook and stir the onion, celery, pepper and mushrooms for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, wine, herbs, garlic and sugar. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes or until chicken is tender. Serve over pasta and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

recipes.Author: Taste of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
3 cups uncooked penne pasta (about 12 ounces)
1 can (28 ounces) whole plum tomatoes
1 lb. bulk Italian sausage
1  medium onion, chopped
1  medium carrot, chopped
1  celery rib, chopped
4  garlic cloves, minced
2 tbsp. tomato paste
1 tsp. dried oregano
½ tsp. salt
½ tsp. dried basil
¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
¼ tsp. pepper
1 can (15 ounces) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
½ cup grated Parmesan cheese, divided
½ cup minced fresh parsley, divided
2 cups shredded fontina or provolone cheese
recipes.Procedure:
Preheat oven to 350°. Cook pasta according to package directions for al dente; drain.
Meanwhile, drain tomatoes, reserving juices; coarsely chop tomatoes. In a 6-qt. stockpot, cook and crumble sausage with onion, carrot, celery and garlic over medium-high heat until no longer pink, 6-8 minutes; drain. Stir in tomato paste, seasonings, chopped tomatoes and reserved juices; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes.
Stir in beans and 1/4 cup each Parmesan cheese and parsley. Stir in pasta. Transfer to a greased 13x9-in. baking dish; sprinkle with fontina cheese and remaining Parmesan cheese.
Bake, covered, 20 minutes. Uncover; bake until cheese is melted, 10-15 minutes. Sprinkle with remaining parsley.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
12  ounces uncooked linguine
2  medium lemons
¼ cup butter, cubed
¼ cup olive oil
8  ounces sliced fresh cremini mushrooms
1  medium onion, chopped
6  garlic cloves, minced
¼ cup sun-dried tomatoes (not packed in oil), julienned
⅔ cup chardonnay
½ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. pepper
¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
1½ lbs.uncooked shrimp (26-30 per pound), peeled and deveined
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
Grated Parmesan cheese, optional
recipes.Procedure:
Cook linguine according to package directions. Meanwhile, halve and thinly slice one lemon. Finely grate peel from remaining lemon; place in small bowl. Cut lemon crosswise in half; squeeze juice into bowl; set aside.
In a 6-qt. stockpot, heat butter and oil over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms, onion and garlic; cook and stir 5 minutes. Add tomatoes, lemon slices, lemon peel and juice; cook 5 minutes longer, stirring occasionally.
Stir in chardonnay, salt, pepper and pepper flakes; cook 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally until wine is evaporated. Add shrimp; cook and stir 4-6 minutes or until shrimp just turn pink.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Drain linguine, reserving 1 cup pasta water. Stir linguine into shrimp mixture, adding enough reserved pasta water to moisten. Heat through. Serve with parsley and, if desired, cheese.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
9  lasagna noodles
1¼ lbs.bulk Italian sausage
¾ lb. ground beef
1  medium onion, diced
3  garlic cloves, minced
2 cans (one 28 ounces, one 15 ounces) crushed tomatoes
2 cans (6 ounces each) tomato paste
⅔ cup water
2  to 3 tbsp. sugar
3 tbsp. plus  ¼ cup minced fresh parsley, divided
2 tsp. dried basil
¾ tsp. fennel seed
¾ tsp. salt, divided
¼ tsp. coarsely ground pepper
1  large egg, lightly beaten
1  carton (15 ounces) ricotta cheese
4 cups shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese
¾ cup grated Parmesan cheese
recipes.Procedure:
Cook noodles according to package directions; drain. Meanwhile, in a Dutch oven, cook sausage, beef and onion over medium heat 8-10 minutes or until meat is no longer pink, breaking up meat into crumbles. Add garlic; cook 1 minute. Drain.
Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, water, sugar, 3 tbsp. parsley, basil, fennel, ½ tsp. salt and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; simmer, uncovered, 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a small bowl, mix egg, ricotta cheese, and remaining parsley and salt.
Preheat oven to 375°. Spread 2 cups meat sauce into an ungreased 13x9-in. baking dish. Layer with three noodles and a third of the ricotta mixture. Sprinkle with 1 cup mozzarella cheese and 2 tbsp. Parmesan cheese. Repeat layers twice. Top with remaining meat sauce and cheeses (dish will be full).
Bake, covered, 25 minutes. Bake, uncovered, 25 minutes longer or until bubbly. Let stand 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup water (70° to 80°)
4½ tsp. olive oil
4½ tsp. sugar
2 tsp. dried oregano
1¼ tsp. salt
3¼ cups bread flour
1½ tsp. active dry yeast
TOPPING:
1 tbsp. olive oil
1 tbsp. dried basil
2  medium tomatoes, thinly sliced
1  medium onion, thinly sliced
1 cup frozen chopped broccoli, thawed
¼ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. pepper
¾ cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 cup shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese
recipes.Procedure:
In bread machine pan, place the first seven ingredients in order suggested by manufacturer. Select dough setting (check dough after 5 minutes of mixing; add 1-2 tbsp. water or flour if needed).
When cycle is completed, turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Punch dough down. Roll into a 13x9-in. rectangle; transfer to a 13x9-in. baking dish coated with cooking spray.
For topping, brush dough with olive oil; sprinkle with basil. Layer with the tomatoes, onion and broccoli; sprinkle with salt, pepper and Parmesan cheese. Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 30 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Sprinkle with mozzarella cheese; bake 10-15 minutes longer or until golden brown and cheese is melted.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
½ lb. Round steak, sliced very thin
4 oz. Snow pea pods
1  Green pepper, chopped into 1" squares
1  Tomato, cut into eighths
½ cup Sliced water chestnuts
½ cup Sliced green onions
½ cup sliced celery
1  clove garlic, minced
1 tbsp. Fresh ginger
2 tbsp. Peanut oil
2 tbsp. Soy sauce
3 tbsp. Dry sherry
recipes.Procedure:
1. Slice water chestnuts, celery, green onions, ginger and green pepper early in day; cover and refrigerate until ready to cook.
2. Heat peanut oil in frying pan or wok.
3. Saute ginger and garlic for 2 minutes.  Add beef and stir fry until just browned. Stir in soy sauce and sherry. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. Add pea pods, celery, peppers and green onions, cook for 3-5 min.  Add tomatoes, cover and cook for 2 min. more. Serve with rice.

recipes.Author: Thewoksoflife.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
4 cups homemade chicken stock
½ tsp. sesame oil
½ tsp. salt
Pinch of sugar
Pinch white pepper
Large pinch of turmeric powder
¼ cup cornstarch mixed with  ½ cup water
3  eggs, slightly beaten
1  scallion, chopped
1 tbsp. cilantro, chopped (optional)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a medium-sized soup pot. Stir in the sesame oil, salt, sugar, and white pepper. Add turmeric. Taste the soup, and adjust the seasoning if needed.
2. Add the cornstarch slurry; make sure the cornstarch and water is mixed well, as the cornstarch settles very quickly. Stir the soup continuously as you drizzle in the slurry, or you’ll get unpleasant clumps of cooked starch in your soup. Use more or less starch if you like a thicker or thinner soup. You can also add the starch in a couple small batches, let the soup simmer for a couple of minutes, then check to see if the consistency is to your liking.
3.Use a ladle to stir the soup in a circular motion, and slowly drizzle in the egg until you have added it all. The speed at which you stir the soup when adding the egg also determines whether you get large “egg flowers” or small egg flowers (i.e. swirly bits of egg). This is more a matter of personal preference than correctness. If you vary the speed at which you stir the soup, you’ll get both. Ladle the soup in a bowl, top with scallion and cilantro, drizzle some sesame oil over the top, and serve.

recipes.Author: Geniuskitchen.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp. cumin
2 tbsp. chili powder
2 tbsp. black pepper
2 tbsp. white pepper
2 tbsp. cayenne pepper
¼ cup dark brown sugar
1 tbsp. sea sealt
2 tbsp. paprika
2 tbsp. garlic powder
2 tbsp. onion powder
Apple cider vinegar (optional)
recipes.Procedure:
Mix dry ingredients.  Prepare ribs by removing membrane from inside of each rack.  Spray ribs with vinegar, and rub generously with the dry mixture.  Cover and let marinate overnight.
This makes rub for 3 racks of spare ribs.

recipes.Ingredients:
24 oz. Mashed potatoes (about 2  ½ cups)
4  eggs
1 tsp. granulated garlic
2 tbsp. fresh chopped chives
1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese
¼ cup shredded/grated Parmesan cheese
6  slices bacon cooked and crumbled
¼ tsp. fresh ground black pepper
¼ tsp. Cayenne pepper
Sour cream chives, cheese and/or crumbled bacon for garnish
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat oven to 400° F. Spray 12 muffin cups generously with nonstick cooking spray. *Very important to spray the pan well to avoid sticking; greasing with butter or vegetable shortening works too.
2. In a large bowl, combine ingredients.
3. Divide the potato mixture evenly into the 12 muffin cups.
4. Bake in the preheated 400 degree oven for 30-35 minutes. Cool slightly before removing each mashed potato puff from its cup. Use a thin knife to loosen if necessary.

Garnish with sour cream, chopped chives, cheese and bacon if desired.

recipes.Ingredients:
4  slices bacon, diced
2 cups vegetable oil, or more, as needed
3 cups leftover mashed potatoes
1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
2 tbsp. chopped fresh chives
½ tsp. cayenne pepper, optional
2  large eggs, beaten
1½ cups Panko crumbs
2 tbsp. freshly grated Parmesan
recipes.Procedure:
1. Heat a large skillet over medium high heat. Add bacon and cook until brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate; set aside.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large stockpot or Dutch oven over medium high heat.
3. In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, cheese, chives, cayenne pepper and bacon.
4. Using a small cookie scoop, roll the mixture into 1 1/4-to-1 1/2-inch balls, forming about 25.
5. Working one at a time, dip balls into eggs, then dredge in Panko, pressing to coat.
6. Working in batches, add balls to the Dutch oven and cook until evenly golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate.
Serve immediately, garnished with Parmesan, if desired.

recipes.Blurb: This recipe is designed for playing around with.  Change anything, or add new ingredients.
recipes.Author: Martha Stewart
recipes.Ingredients:
12  ounces linguine
12  ounces cherry or grape tomatoes, halved or quartered if large
1  onion, thinly sliced (about 2 cups)
4  cloves of garlic, thinly sliced
½ tsp. red pepper flakes
2  sprigs basil, plus torn leaves for garnish
2 tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
Coarse salt
Freshly ground black pepper
4½ cups water
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, for serving
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine pasta, tomatoes, onion, garlic, red-pepper flakes, basil, oil, 2 teaspoons salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, and water in a large straight-sided skillet (the linguine should lay flat). 
2. Bring to a boil over high heat. Boil mixture, stirring and turning pasta frequently with tongs or a fork, until pasta is al dente and water has nearly evaporated, about 9 minutes. 
2. Season to taste with salt and pepper, divide among 4 bowls, and garnish with basil. Serve with olive oil and Parmesan.

recipes.Ingredients:
¾ lb. uncooked large shrimp, peeled and deveined
½ cup lemon juice
¼ cup butter, melted
2 tbsp. vegetable oil
2 tbsp. Dijon mustard
1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce
3  cloves garlic, minced
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large resealable bag, combine lemon juice, butter, oil, mustard, Worcestershire suace and garlic.  Add shrimp, seal bag and turn to coat.  Refrigerate for 4 hours, turning occasionally.
2. Drain and discard marinade.  Sauté shrimp in large pan on medium high until the shrimp are pink: about 4 minutes.  Serve with rice pilaf.

recipes.Author: Penzey's
recipes.Ingredients:
4 cups milk
3 tbsp. sugar
2 tbsp. cocoa
dash ground cinnamon
several drops vanilla extract
recipes.Procedure: Mix ingredients in a sauce pan and warm gently.  Do not boil.

recipes.Blurb: This is the recipe from the movie "Chef".
recipes.Author: Roy Choi
recipes.Ingredients:
2  thin sliced baked ham
4  large thin slices Mojo Pork
6  inch slice of a baguette, sliced in half lengthwise
melted butter
mustard
2  slices Swiss cheese
2  dill pickles, thinly sliced.
recipes.Procedure:
1. Heat skillet over medium heat.  Add ham and pork slices and cook until slightly browned, and remove to a plate.
2. Butter cut sides of baguette and place in the skillet, cut side down, for 2 minutes until lightly browned.
3.  Layer the bottom of the baguette with pork and ham, then cheese and pickles.  Cut, break or fold the meat and cheese so they fit.  Spread the cut side of the bun tops with mustard then place on sandwich.
4.  Butter top and bottom outsides of the baguette.
5.  Heat skillet over high heat.  Place baguette in the skillet, cover with baking paper and weigh it down with a heavy skillet or pot.  Cook for 3 min. on each side until dark golden brown and crispy, and the cheese is melted.  Serve immediately.

recipes.Blurb: This is the recipe from the movie "Chef".
recipes.Author: Roy Choi
recipes.Ingredients:
Marinade:
¾ cup extra virgin olive oil
1 cup cilantro/coriander, lightly packed
1 tbsp. orange zest or peel
¾ cup orange juice, fresh
½ cup lime juice
¼ cup mint leaves, lightly packed
8  cloves garlic
1 tbsp. fresh oregano or  ½ tbsp. dried
2 tsp. ground cumin
1 tsp. salt
1 tsp. black pepper
4 lb. pork shoulder or loin
For the sauce:
2 tbsp. lime juice
¼ cup orange juice
salt and pepper
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine Marinade ingredients in a food processor and blend until the herbs and garlic are finely chopped. Alternatively, you can finely chop/mince the garlic and herbs then mix all ingredients in a bowl.
2. Place in a large ziplock bag with the pork. Place in the fridge overnight (in a bowl, just to be safe).
3. Remove the pork from the Marinade and bring to room temperature. Reserve the Marinade.
4. Preheat oven to 325°.
5. Place the pork on a rack in a roasting dish (or on a couple of onions, halved, to elevate the pork). Cover with a lid or double layer or foil, slightly tented so it is not pressed tightly against the pork.
6. Place in the oven and bake for 2 hrs 30 minutes. Then remove the foil and return to the oven for a further 30 minutes to brown.
7. Remove from the oven and place on a plate, loosely covered with foil. Rest for 20 minutes before serving with the Mojo Sauce on the side.

recipes.Ingredients:
For sauce:
2 tbsp. oyster sauce
2 tbsp. water
1 tbsp. rice wine
1 tbsp. brown sugar
1 tbsp. cornstarch
For broccoli beef:
1 lb. flank steak thinly sliced
1 tbsp. cornstarch
2 tbsp. rice wine
1 lb. broccoli florets
2 tbsp. cooking oil plus a splash of sesame oil
2 tsp. minced garlic
¼ tsp. minced ginger
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Prepare sauce by combining all ingredients in a small bowl, and set aside.
2.  Mix cornstarch and rice wine and pour over sliced beef.  Stir well to coat; marinate for at least 1 hour.
3.  Steam broccoli just until it turns bright green.
4.  Heat wok or skillet until very hot.  Pour in oil an swirl around.  Lay meant in one layer and cook until browned; turn beef slices, add garlic and ginger and mix quickly.  Add broccoli.  Give the finishing sauce a quick stir and pour it over the beef and broccoli.  Stir until sauce thickens.  Serve over rice.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
8  Roma tomatoes, peeled
½  small onion
1  serrano pepper
1  small habanero pepper
1  clove garlic
1 tbsp. cilantro, dried or chopped
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Process the peppers, onion and garlic in a food processor until finely chopped.
2.  Sauté peppers and onions just until onion becomes translucent.
3.  Return pepper and onion mixture to food processor.  Add tomatoes and cilantrol.  Process only until tomatoes are just chopped.  Chill to let flavors blend.

recipes.Author: Adapted From Joy Of
recipes.Ingredients:
3½ cups all-purpose flour
2 tsp. salt
2 tbsp. baking powder
6 tbsp. unsalted butter
5 tbsp. dried buttermilk powder
1-1/3 cup water
recipes.Procedure: Place flour, salt, baking powder, buttermilk powder and butter into food processor.  Process until  the butter is fully blended with flour (flour will be dense).  While processor is running, slowly add water.  Continue processing until dough forms a ball (add additional water, a little at a time, if dough is too dry to form ball).  Remove from food processor and roll on lightly floured surface to a thickness of 3/4 in.  Cut with biscuit cutter, taking care not to twist the cutter.  Place biscuits on ungreased baking sheet and bake at 450º for 12-15 min.  Brush the biscuits with melted butter after the first 7 min of baking and, if desired, again after 9 min.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
2  Chicken thighs, meat removed and cut into bite-sized pieces
2½ tbsp. olive oil
1 cup fresh chicken stock
Chopped onion
Salt and pepper
1½ tsp. marjoram
1½ tsp. Italian parsley
recipes.Procedure: Brown chicken in olive oil.  Cover with chopped onions, parsely and marjoram.  Add salt and pepper to taste.  Pour in broth; cover lightly and simmer until thickened.  Serve over buttermilk biscuits.

recipes.Ingredients:
1  whole chicken
1 tsp. sea salt
½ tsp. paprika
½ tsp. dried oregano
½ tsp. white pepper
¼ tsp. cayenne
½ tsp. black pepper
2 tbsp. olive oil
1  onion, quartered
recipes.Procedure: Place quartered onion in chicken cavity.  Mix seasonings with olive oil; brush chicken with mixture.  Place on wire rack in backing dish and bake at 250º until interior temperature reaches 165º (about 4 hours).  Remove from oven and let rest about 10 min. before slicing.

recipes.Author: Kenzi Wilbur
recipes.Ingredients:
10 tbsp. unsalted butter
1½  lbs.yellow onions halved and sliced  ¼" thick
1 tbsp. sugar
pinch kosher salt
¼ cup Madeira
¾ lb. hot cooked pasta
grated Parmesan
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large (12-inch) skillet, warm the butter over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are soft and translucent.
2. Stir in the sugar and a pinch of salt, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the onions slowly for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Patience is key! When they're done, they should be dark, caramelized, and borderline jammy. 
3. Stir in the Madeira, cook for a few more minutes, and then add the cooked pasta to the pan. Shower on a generous dusting of Parmesan, and using two large spoons, toss the pasta well with the sauce.
4. Serve with additional grated Parmesan, and flaky salt if necessary.

recipes.Author: Mel's Kitchen Cafe
recipes.Ingredients:
3¾ cups all-purpose flour (see note)
½ cup whole wheat flour
¼ cup nonfat dry milk
2 tsp. yeast
2 tsp. salt
2 tbsp. oil
1½ cups lukewarm water, enough to make a smooth, soft dough
recipes.Procedure:
1. Let yeast dissolve in warm water until creamy, about 5 minutes. Add the rest of the ingredients—by hand, mixer or bread machine— and knead till you've created a smooth dough.
2. Allow the dough to rise, covered, for 45 minutes; it should become puffy. Divide the dough into 5-6 pieces, depending on how large you want your bread bowl to be. Roll each piece into a ball. Place on a lightly greased or parchment covered baking sheet.
3. Cover the bread bowls with greased plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 4 hours (or up to 24 hours); this step will give the bread bowls extra flavor, and a delightfully crisp-chewy texture. Two or more hours before serving, remove the bread bowls from the refrigerator. Uncover, and let them sit for about one hour while you preheat the oven to 425°F.
4. Just before baking, slash the top surface of the bowls several times with a sharp razor/knife to allow them to expand. Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the bowls are deep brown, and sound hollow when thumped on the bottom. Remove from the oven, and cool on a rack.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
1½ lbs.potatoes (about 3 medium), peeled and diced
¼ tsp. baking soda
3 tbsp. butter
1  small onion, finely chopped
3 tbsp. all-purpose flour
3½ cups whole milk
4  ounces process cheese (Velveeta), cubed (about 1 cup)
½ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
1½ cups cubed fully cooked ham
Minced chives and coarsely ground pepper, optional
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place potatoes and baking soda in a large saucepan. Add water to cover; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cook, uncovered, until potatoes are tender, 6-8 minutes. Drain, reserving ½ cup potato water. 
2. In same pan, heat butter over medium heat; saute onion until tender, 2-4 minutes. Stir in flour until blended; cook and stir 2 minutes. Gradually stir in milk and reserved potato water. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly; cook and stir until thickened, 1-2 minutes. 
3. Stir in cheeses until melted. Stir in ham and potatoes; heat through. serve in bread bowls. If desired, sprinkle with chives and pepper.

recipes.Blurb: It's a good idea to make the brine the day before, as it takes a long time to cool, and must be cold before brining the fish.
recipes.Author: Smoker-Cooking.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
¾ cup canning salt or 1 cup kosher salt
1 clove garlic, crushed
1  bayleaf, dried or fresh
½ tbsp. black peppercorns, cracked
1 tbsp. onion powder
1 tbsp. Old Bay seasoning
½ gallon water
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine all ingredients in a large pan and bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 min., cover and cool to room temperature. Try to float an egg in the brine. If it doesn't float, mix in another 1/8 cup salt and test again. Repeat until the egg floats. Refrigerate brine to 40° or less.
2. Immerse salmon fillet in brine. Leave for 6-12 hours. Use less time for thinner fillets, or if the salmon was previously frozen.
3. Rinse fillet by placing in a clean container and allow water to run through the container for 30 min. Test salmon for saltiness. If too salty, rinse for another 10-15 min. but no longer.
4. Place fillet on a rack and refrigerate, uncovered, for 12 hours. Add spices or herbs at this point, if desired.
5. Smoke salmon for 12-16 hours. Use alder wood, or your favorite. You must use a non-heat generating smoke generator. DO NOT let salmon get above 80° F. during smoking.
6. Package salmon in a vacuum sealed bag for storage.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Hom
recipes.Ingredients:
2  large onions, finely chopped
2 tbsp. olive oil
¾ cup sour cream
¾ cup plain Greek yogurt
3 tsp. onion powder
½ tsp. salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large skillet, saute onions in oil until softened. Reduce heat to medium-low; cook, stirring occasionally, for 30 minutes or until deep golden brown. Cool completely. 
2. In a small bowl, combine the sour cream, yogurt, onion powder and salt; stir in two-thirds cooked onions. Transfer to a serving bowl; top with remaining onions. Serve with chips and vegetables.

recipes.Author: Allrecipes.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
⅓ cup butter
½ tsp. ground black pepper
1 tsp. garlic powder
2  lbs.skinless, boneless chicken breast halves
2  eggs
3 tbsp. water
¼ tsp. ground black pepper
½ tsp. garlic powder
1 tsp. dried dill weed
¾ cup all-purpose flour
¾ cup dry bread crumbs
2 cups vegetable oil for frying
½  lemon, sliced
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine 1/3 cup butter, 1/2 teaspoon pepper and 1 teaspoon garlic powder. On a 6x6 inch piece of aluminum foil, spread mixture to about 2x3 inches. Place this mixture in the coldest section of your freezer and freeze until firm. This can be done ahead of time.
2. Remove all fat from the chicken breast. If using whole chicken breasts, cut them in half. Place each chicken breast half between 2 pieces of waxed paper and using a mallet, pound carefully to about 1/4 inch thickness or less.
3. When butter mixture is firm, remove from freezer and cut into 6 equal pieces. Place one piece of butter on each chicken breast. Fold in edges of chicken and then roll to encase the butter completely. Secure the chicken roll with small skewers or toothpicks.
4. In a mixing bowl, beat eggs with water until fluffy. In a separate bowl, mix together 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, dill weed and flour. Coat the chicken well with the seasoned flour. Dip the floured chicken in the egg mixture and then roll in the bread crumbs. Place coated chicken on a shallow tray and chill in refrigerator for 30 minutes.
5. In a medium size deep frying pan, heat vegetable oil to medium-high. Fry chicken for about 5 minutes then turn over and fry for 5 minutes longer or until the chicken is golden brown. To test for doneness, cut into one of the rolled chicken breasts to make sure it doesn't have a pink interior. Serve immediately, garnished with a sliced lemon twist and a sprinkling or parsley.

recipes.Ingredients:
4 cups broccoli florets
3 tbsp. olive oil
½ tsp. Italian seasoning or equal parts garlic powder, dried oregano and dried basil
salt and pepper to taste
3 tbsp. finely grated parmesan cheese
1 tbsp. chopped fresh parsley
1 tbsp. lemon juice
cooking spray
lemon wedges optional garnish
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees. Coat a sheet pan with cooking spray.
2. Place the broccoli florets in a gallon sized freezer bag. Add the olive oil, Italian seasoning and salt and pepper to taste.
3. Seal the bag and shake to coat evenly.
4. Pour the broccoli onto the sheet pan in a single layer.
5. Bake for 20 minutes, stirring halfway through.
6. Remove the pan from the oven. Sprinkle the parmesan and parsley over the broccoli and drizzle with lemon juice, then serve, garnished with lemon wedges if desired.

recipes.Blurb: This can be easily doubled or halved.  Use on beef, pork, chicken and turkey.
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup water
4 tbsp. buttermilk powder
2 tsp. kosher salt
recipes.Procedure:
1) Warm water in microwave to about 80° in a measuring cup.
2) Add buttermilk powder and salt and whisk together.
3) Chill before using to marinate cold meat.

recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp. Olive Oil
4  cloves Garlic, Minced
1  Medium Onion, Diced
1 can (28 oz. Size) Peeled Whole Tomatoes
3  Tablespoons Tomato Paste
⅓ cup Brown Sugar
1 tbsp. Molasses
⅓ cup Apple Cider Vinegar
1  Tablespoon Worcestershire Sauce
½ tsp. Chili Powder
¼ tsp. Powdered Ginger
¼ tsp. Ground Allspice
¼ tsp. Cinnamon
recipes.Procedure:
1. Heat a 4-quart sauce pot over medium high heat. Add olive oil and onions, sauté until translucent, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes. 
2. Add tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, molasses and cider vinegar. Bring to a slow boil, lower to a simmer and using a spoon crush the whole tomatoes. Add remaining ingredients and continue to simmer, uncovered for 45–55 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very thick. Make sure to keep an eye on it and stir it to keep it from scorching. 
3. Process in a blender until smooth. (Optional: Strain through a fine mesh strainer.) Chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours. The ketchup will continue to develop flavor and thicken.

recipes.Author: Madame Wong
recipes.Ingredients:
2  whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into  ½ in. cubes
½ tsp. sea salt
2 cups oil for deep frying
½ cup dry-roasted peanuts
2  green onions, cut into  ½ in. lengths
2  cloves garlic, minced.
1 cup all-purpose flour
⅛ tsp. cayenne
8 oz. buttermilk
For the sauce:
2 tsp. chili paste
2 tbsp. soy sauce
1 tbsp. sherry
1 tsp. red wine vinegar
1 tsp. sugar
¼ cup salt-free chicken stock
1 tsp. cornstarch
1 tsp. sesame seed oil
recipes.Procedure:
1. Marinate chicken pieces in buttermilk, to which 1 tsp sea salt and ¼ tsp black pepper has been added, for 4-6 hours.  Drain.
2.  Roll chicken pieces in a mixture of all-purpose flour and cayenne.  Refrigrate for 30 minutes until dry.
3. In a small bowl, blend sauce ingredients.  Set aside.
4.  Deep-fry chicken pieces until lightly browned.
5.  Stir-fry green onions and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 1 minute.  Add chicken pieces; stir-fry 1 minute.  Pour sauce over chicken.  Stir-fry until thoroughly heated and glazed.  Add peanuts.

recipes.Author: Shaheen Ali
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup Rice , semi-cooked
2 tbsp. Olive Oil
1  Onion , chopped
1  Carrot, chopped
3  cloves Garlic , crushed
1 tsp. Orange Zest (Rind)
½ tsp. Dried Thyme Leaves
½ tsp. Fennel Powder
½ cup Homemade tomato puree
2 cups Lukewarm Water
2  Tomatoes , chopped
1 cup Vegetable stock
1 tsp. Salt
1 tsp. Sugar
recipes.Procedure:
1. Heat oil in a Saucepan and saute onions, carrot, garlic, orange zest, thyme and add fennel powder.
Once the vegetables start to soften, add tomato paste and water. Mix well till everything is incorporated well.
2. Add in the chopped tomatoes now along with vegetable stock and season with salt, pepper and sugar.
3. As it starts boiling add semi cooked white rice. Close the lid and simmer for around 12-15 minutes until the rice is tender.
4. Pour the soup into bowls, add a swirl of fresh cream and garnish with fresh basil and crushed dry thyme and serve Provençal Tomato Rice Soup Recipe with salad of your choice.

recipes.Author: Robert Irvine
recipes.Ingredients:
¼ cup grapeseed oil
8  lbs.veal bones (joints preferred)
6  quarts ice water
8  ounces onions, roughly chopped
4  ounces carrots, peeled and roughly chopped
4  ounces celery, roughly chopped
6  ounces tomato paste
5  sprigs fresh thyme
1  bay leaf
2  quarts red wine
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F. 
2. Pour the oil into a metal roasting pan and put it in the preheated oven for 3 to 5 minutes to heat up the pan and condition it with the oil. Spread the bones out on the roasting pan and cook until browned, 30 to 45 minutes, turning the bones occasionally so they brown evenly. 
3. Transfer the bones to a large-enough stockpot to accommodate the bones, 6 quarts ice water and more. Use tongs to transfer the bones so you do not pour any fat into the stockpot. Add the ice water to the stockpot and bring to a simmer. Allow the stock to cook for 4 hours at a slow simmer. Skim the surface of the stock occasionally to remove any fat or impurities. 
4. While the stock is simmering, discard all but about 1/4 cup of the fat from the roasting pan. Bring the pan back up to temperature over high heat on the stovetop. Add the onions and carrots and cook until golden brown and caramelized. Add the celery and cook for another 10 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, thyme and bay leaf and cook, stirring regularly, until the tomato paste gets a brick red color, about 15 minutes. Add 1 cup of the red wine and stir it into the mirepoix (vegetable) mixture. 
5. Add the mirepoix mixture to the stock after the 4-hour simmering time. Bring the stock back up to a simmer and continue to cook it for another 2 hours. 
6. In a separate pot, bring the remaining 7 cups red wine to a boil and cook until reduced by half, 15 to 20 minutes. 
7. When the stock has simmered for 6 hours, strain it through a chinois and combine the strained stock with the reduced red wine. Bring the stock to a boil, lower the heat to a hard simmer and reduce the stock until it has a consistency that coats the back of spoon and is about 2 quarts (8 cups) in volume, up to 1 hour. Season with salt and pepper and then strain the sauce though a chinois again.

recipes.Author: Chef John
recipes.Ingredients:
¼ cup olive oil
1  onion, finely diced
1  rib celery, finely diced
1  pinch salt
4  cloves garlic, minced
2  (28 ounce) cans whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes
2 tsp. white sugar
1 tsp. salt
1 tsp. anchovy paste
1 tsp. white wine vinegar
½ tsp. dried Italian herbs
1  pinch red pepper flakes
1 tbsp. tomato paste
2 tbsp. chopped Italian flat-leaf parsley
water, or as needed
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place olive oil, onion, celery, and a pinch of salt into a large heavy saucepan or Dutch oven over medium-low heat. Cook until onions are very soft, about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Mix garlic into onion mixture and cook just until fragrant, about 1 more minute.
2. Pour tomatoes and their juice into a large mixing bowl and use your hands to crush the tomatoes until they look pureed.
3. Mix sugar, 1 teaspoon salt, anchovy paste, white wine vinegar, Italian herbs, and red pepper flakes into vegetable mixture. Raise heat to medium and cook just until liquid has evaporated. Stir in tomato paste and bring to a simmer. Pour in San Marzano tomatoes and parsley. Bring sauce to a simmer, turn heat to low, and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, adding a little water as the sauce cooks down. Stir occasionally.

recipes.Ingredients:
1 lb. fresh Tabasco, or other hot peppers
2 cup distilled white vinegar (top quality)
1½ tsp. salt
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Wash peppers and remove stems.  Chop coarsely with a knife or food processor.
2.  Place chopped peppers in saucepan.  Add vinegar and salt.  Bring to a boil over med-high heat.  Reduce heat to low, simmer 5 min.  (Use timer.)  Remove from heat immediately. Cover pan loosely and allow sauce to cool completely.
3.  Puree the pepper mixture in a blender.  Pour sauce into airtight bottle and refrigerate for two weeks.
4.  Strain sauce through a fine mesh strainer, into a pan.  Discard the pepper pulp.  Bottle sauce.

recipes.Blurb: This is a pressure-cooker recipe.
recipes.Author: Cuisinart
recipes.Ingredients:
3 tbsp. olive oil
2  lbs.lean ground beef or sausage
1½ cups chopped onion
¾ cup finely chopped carrot
⅓ cup finely chopped celery
2  cloves garlic, peeled
2 tsp. basil
½ cup dry wine (red or white)
3 cans (14-15 oz.) diced tomatoes
1 can (6 oz.) tomato paste (salt free is best)
½ cup water
1  bay leaf
1 tsp. kosher salt
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Add 1 tbsp oil to pressure cooker.  Select Browning and let oil heat 3-4 min.  Cook meat in 4 batches, breaking up meat with a wooden spoon until browned; 3-5 min.  Move meat as little as possible while browning.  Remove to a bowl as meat is browned.
2. Select Sauté. Add chopped onion, carrots, celery, garlic and basil to the cooking pot.  Cook, stirring for 2-3 min. until the onion becomes translucent and basil  becomes aromatic.
3.  Stir in wine and cook for 2-3 min to reduce by about half.  Add tomaotes, tomato paste, water, bay leaf and salt to the cooking pot and stir.
4.  Return the ground beef and any juices to the pot.  Turn off.
5.  Cover and lock lid in place.  Select High Pressure and set timer for 20 min.  When beep sounds, use natural pressure release..  Remove and discard bay leaf before serving.

recipes.Ingredients:
½ cup milk
1 cup sifted flour
1½ tsp. baking powder
⅛ tsp. salt
2  eggs
1 cup granulated sugar
1 tsp. vanilla extract
CREAM FILLING
½ cup granulated sugar
¼ cup cornstarch
¼ tsp. salt
2 cup milk
4  egg yolks
½ tsp. vanilla extract
CHOCOLATE GLAZE
2 tbsp. butter or margarine
1  square unsweetened chocolate
1 cup sifted confectioner's sugar
2 tbsp. boiling water
recipes.Procedure:
1. Make Spongecake. Preheat oven to 350° F. Heat ½ cup milk in small saucepan until bubbles form around edge. Remove from heat and cool slightly. Sift flour with baking powder and 1/8 tsp. salt and set aside. In small bowl of electric mixer at high speed beat 2 eggs until thick and lemon colored. Gradually add 1 cup granulated sugar, ¼ cup at a time, beating until mixture is thick and smooth - about 5 minutes. Add 1 tsp. vanilla At low speed, blend in flour mixture just until smooth. Add warm milk beating until just blended. Pour into an ungreased 9 inch round layer cake pan. Bake 30 - 35 minutes or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean. Remove from oven and invert cake; cool completely.
2. Meanwhile, make cream filling. In medium saucepan, conbine egg yolks and sugar. Mix until smooth. Add cornstarch, salt, vanilla and about about ¼ cup of the milk. Stir until well mixed. Gradually stir in remaining milk. Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens--it will thicken suddenly. Do not allow to boil! Remove from heat, cover with plastic wrap directly touching filling and refrigerate.
3. Make chocolate glaze - in small bowl, over hot water, melt butter and chocolate. Remove bowl from water and let it cool. Add confectioners sugar and boiling water, beat just until smooth and well combined. 4. Remove cooled spongecake from pan and split into two even layers. Place bottom layer cut side up on a serving plate and spread with cooled cream filling. Top with remaining layer cut side down. Spread glaze over top. Refrigerate if not serving immediately. Keep remainder not served in refrigerator.
HIgh altitude: Reduce baking powder to 1 1/8 tsp. Add 1 tbsp. extra milk. Add 1 tbsp. extra flour. Bake at 300º for 45 min.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
4  boneless, skinless chicken breasts
3 tbsp. soy sauce, divided
2 tbsp. white wine (or rice wine)
2 tsp. minced ginger
1  clove of garlic, minced
¼ cup plus 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, divided
Canola oil, for frying
1 tbsp. honey
⅔ cup orange juice
1 tbsp. orange marmalade
1 tbsp. rice vinegar
¼ tsp. crushed red chili flakes
¼ tsp. sesame oil
recipes.Procedure:
1. Cut the chicken into small, bite-size pieces—about 1 to 1-1/2 inches long. Then, whisk together two tablespoons of soy sauce, wine, ginger and garlic in a large bowl. Add the chicken and stir until the pieces are well coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 25 minutes.
2. Once time is up, use a large slotted spoon to move the chicken cubes out of the marinade and into a new bowl. Discard the marinade mixture. Then, sprinkle 1/4 cup of cornstarch over the chicken. Toss lightly to coat.
3. Heat up the oil to fry the chicken pieces in a large pot—between 1/4- and 1/3-inch of oil will be enough. Then, working in batches, add a single layer of marinated chicken pieces to the hot oil. Fry, turning occasionally until the chicken is well-browned and cooked through. Each batch should take about four minutes, total. When cooked through, move the chicken pieces out of the fryer and onto a paper towel-lined plate so the excess oil can drain away.
4. Place a small saucepan over medium heat and add the remaining soy sauce, honey, orange juice, marmalade, rice vinegar, chili flakes, and sesame oil. Stir to combine. Then, in a small bowl, mix together the remaining cornstarch and two tablespoons water. This mixture is called a slurry. Bring the orange sauce to a low boil, and add the slurry—one spoonful at a time—while whisking. Keep adding the slurry until the sauce is thickened.
5. Combine the chicken pieces and the sauce in a large bowl. Serve with cooked rice and broccoli.

recipes.Blurb: This is a copycat version of the Annie's Naturals dressing.
recipes.Author: Adapted From Letty's Kitchen
recipes.Ingredients:
2  dried shiitake mushrooms
1½ tsp. roasted sesame seeds
1 cup canola oil
⅓ cup apple cider vinegar
2 tbsp. and 2 tsp. tamari soy sauce
1½ tsp. sesame oil
¼ tsp. xanthan gum powder, optional
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place mushrooms in vinegar. Let soak until the mushrooms are soft, about 10 minutes. If using raw sesame seeds, toast the sesame seeds in a small skillet, stirring until they are golden in color.
2. In a blender jar, put the oil, vinegar and mushrooms, soy sauce, sesame oil, and xanthan gum, if using. Whir about 10 seconds, just until the mushrooms are tiny pieces. Add the toasted sesame seeds and blend a few seconds more.
3. Store in a glass jar, refrigerated.

recipes.Ingredients:
For meatballs:
1 lb. lean ground beef
1 lb. lean ground pork
2  eggs
1  small onion, finely diced
½ cup breadcrumbs or I Kaiser roll (see hints below)
1½ tsp. salt
½ tsp. pepper
For sauce:
6 cups chicken stock (or use water and bouillon cubes)
1  bay leaf
½ tsp. black peppercorns
4 tbsp. flour
3 tbsp. cider vinegar
1 tbsp. lemon juice
2 tbsp. capers
1 cup sour cream
salt and pepper
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large bowl, gently mix all ingredients. Shape into golf-ball sized meatballs.
2. Bring stock to boil. Add bay leaf and peppercorns.
Gently add uncooked meatballs and lower heat to a simmer. Gently simmer for about 15 minutes or until meatballs are cooked through.
3. Remove meatballs to a bowl and cover to keep warm.
4. Discard bay leaf from stock. Return sauce (stock) to simmer. Mix flour with a bit of cold water to make a slurry and add to sauce, stirring until thickened (about 5 minutes.)
5. Stir in cider vinegar and lemon juice. Add capers. 
6. Remove from heat and add sour cream and season with salt and pepper.
7. Return meatballs to sauce and return to heat if needed.  Do not allow to boil.

recipes.Blurb: Choose stock or milk, depending on the consistency of the sauce you desire.  Milk will yield a thicker sauce.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
3 tbsp. butter
3 tbsp. all-purpose flour
1 cup chicken stock or milk, chilled
1 tbsp. lemon juice
1 cup cubed Velveeta cheese, at room temperature.
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Melt the butter in a saucepan.  Stir in flour.  Cook briefly, but do not allow the roux to brown.
2. Add the chicken stock or milk and bring to a boil; if using milk, heat to a high simmer only. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
3.  Sprinkle the lemon juice over the cheese cubes.  Add cheese cubes and stir until melted.  Serve at once.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup sourdough starter
6 oz. water
3 cups bread flour
2 tsp. dried milk
1 tsp. salt
3 tsp. active dry yeast
recipes.Procedure:
1. Starter should be quite liquid. Add more water if necessary--dough should be fairly wet, yet able to hold a shape. Pour starter and 6 oz. water into bread pan. Add flour, dried milk and salt. Make a small well in middle of flour and add yeast to it. Process on dough cycle.
2. When dough is finished, divide into two equal pieces. Handling the dough as little as possible, shape each piece into a baguette shape. Place on parchment-lined baking sheet, or baguette sheet, spray with water and allow to double in size. Meanwhile, preheat oven to 425º.
3. Make a slash down the center of each baguette. Add two cups of ice cubes to the bottom of the oven and immediately place baking sheet in oven. Bake for 25 min. Remove and cool completely on wire rack.

recipes.Author: Thespruceeats.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup all-purpose flour
1  large egg
1 cup water
Ice cubes (for chilling the water)`
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a small bowl, sift the flour once or twice to remove any clumps and to make it light and soft. Set aside.
2. In a separate medium bowl, gently beat 1 egg until the yolk and egg whites are just barely incorporated.
3. Combine the water and ice cubes in a cup. Using a strainer, strain the water (you should have 1 cup of ice-cold water) and add it to the bowl with the beaten egg. Make sure you do not actually add ice cubes to the tempura batter mixture.
4. Add the sifted flour into the bowl with the egg and water mixture and lightly combine the flour using chopsticks. Be careful not to overmix the batter.
5. Lightly coat the seafood or vegetable in either cake flour, Wondra flour, or all-purpose flour before dipping them into the tempura batter. This allows the batter to adhere better. Once coated, dip your items into the batter gently. You don't want too much batter, otherwise, you run the risk of the outside being crispy but the inside being mushy. When ready to fry, make sure that your frying oil is between 340 F and 360 F. Any higher and it will be too crispy. Any lower and it the tempura will absorb too much oil and won't get crispy enough.

recipes.Blurb: The traditional Japanese dipping sauce for shrimp or vegetable tempura. Serve in small bowls at each setting. Optionally, provide grated fresh ginger and grated daikon to mix into sauce.
recipes.Author: Allrecipes.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup water
1 tbsp. dashi granules
¼ cup mirin (Japanese sweet wine)
2 tbsp. soy sauce
recipes.Procedure: In a small saucepan, bring water to a boil. Stir in dashi, and cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat, and stir in mirin and soy sauce.

recipes.Blurb: This is a copy-cat version of Arby Sauce
recipes.Author: Copykat.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup Water
½ cup ketchup
2 tbsp. Brown Sugar
¼ cup White Vinegar
¾ tsp. Onion Powder
¾ tsp. Garlic Powder
½ tsp. Paprika
3 tbsp. Worcestershire Sauce (Lea and Perrins)
⅛ tsp. Salt
⅛ tsp. Cayenne Pepper
Corn Starch Mixture (thickening mixture)
1 tbsp. Corn Starch
2 tbsp. Water
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place all sauce ingredients in a blender and blend on high speed for 15 - 20 seconds. Pour ingredients into a small saucepan, heat on medium low. Simmer gently for twenty minutes, stirring several times. 
2. After twenty minutes add cornstarch mixture, stir well. When sauce begins to thickens let simmer on a very low temperature for ten minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.

recipes.Author: Cook.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
1  -2 tbsp. lemon zest, about 3 lemons
2  -3 tbsp. black peppercorns
1 tbsp. sea salt
recipes.Procedure: Dry zest, if fresh, in oven.  Mix zest, peppercorns and salt in spice grider; process until mixed, but pepper remains slightly coarse.

recipes.Author: Allrecipes.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
2½ cups bread flour
1¼ tsp. salt
1 cup water, or as needed
1 cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
recipes.Procedure:
1. Mix the flour and salt together in a large bowl or in the bowl of a stand mixer that is fitted with a dough hook. Gradually stir in water until the dough holds together enough to clean the sides of the bowl. You may not need the full amount of water. Shape into a flat ball, and allow to rest for at least 10 minutes.
2. Place the butter between two pieces of plastic wrap and pound into a flat disc using a rolling pin or other heavy object. Refrigerate until firm, about 20 minutes.
3. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough into a large rectangle about 1/2 inch thick. Place the disc of chilled butter in the center and fold the two ends over it so that it is completely encased in dough. Roll out the dough again, taking care not to let the butter break through the dough, to about 1/2 inch thickness. Fold into thirds. This is the first ''turn''. Rotate the dough 90 degrees and roll out into a rectangle again. Fold into thirds. By this time the butter is starting to warm up. Place the dough on a baking sheet and mark it with two pokes from your finger (two turns). Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
4. Repeat this rolling, folding and turning two more times, then refrigerate until firm. Repeat two more times for a total of 6 ''turns''. Wrap and refrigerate. The dough is now ready to roll out and use in any recipe calling for puff pastry. Roll the dough out as thin as 1/4 inch to make pastries. Bake in a preheated oven of at least 400° to get the maximum puff from your pastry.

recipes.Ingredients:
2  cloves garlic, sliced
¼ tsp. red pepper flakes
¼ tsp. dry oregano leaves
12  whole peppercorns
1  (14oz.) jar baby artichoke hearts packed in water, drained
½ cup water
½ cup Apple Cider Vinegar
olive oil (approximately ¼ cup)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Into a clean 16-24 ounce jar put the garlic, red pepper flakes, dry oregano leaves and peppercorns.
Add the artichoke hearts.
2. Measure the water and cider vinegar into a small sauce pot. Heat to a boil over high heat. Pour over the artichoke hearts until 3/4 covered in liquid. You may not need all of the liquid depending on the size of your jar.
3. Pour olive oil over the artichoke hearts until they are fully covered.
4. Put on the lid and shake well. Cool on the counter. Refrigerate for 24 hours before serving. They’ll keep in the fridge for 1 week.

recipes.Author: Food.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. fruity olive oil
2  garlic cloves, thinly sliced
1 tbsp. fresh rosemary, coarsely chopped
1 tbsp. dried thyme
1 tsp. hot pepper flakes
2 cups large green olives
2 cups kalamata olives
1 tsp. coarsely grated lemon peel
recipes.Procedure:
1. Over medium heat, warm oil in a large skillet.
Add garlic and cook, stirring often, for 3 minutes until fragrant. Remove garlic and discard
2. Add rosemary, thyme and hot pepper flakes. Cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
3. Add olives, continue to stir and cook for only 2 or 3 minutes, just until until olives are warm.
4. Stir in lemon peel.

recipes.Blurb: These olives benefit from a long refrigeration before eating.
recipes.Author: Tasteofhome.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
1  jar (7 ounces) pimiento-stuffed olives
½ cup tomato juice
1 tbsp. olive oil
½  to 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
2  garlic cloves, minced
½ tsp. dried basil
½ tsp. dried oregano
recipes.Procedure: Drain olives, discarding juice; return olives to the jar. In a small bowl, combine the remaining ingredients. Pour over olives; cover and refrigerate for 3-10 days, turning jar daily. Drain before serving.

recipes.Blurb: Substitue wild mushrooms for the white mushrooms, or try a different hard cheese.
recipes.Author: Michele Scicolone
recipes.Ingredients:
12 oz. white mushrooms, sliced paper-thin
2  tender celery ribs, sliced paper-thin
2  medium carrots, sliced paper-thin
⅔ cup extra-virgin olive oil
2  to 3 tbsp. fresh lemon juice
salt, to taste
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Small wedge of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
recipes.Procedure:
1.  On a large platter, toss together mushrooms, celergy and carrots.
2. Whisk together oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.  Pour over salad and toss well.
3.  With a vegetable peeler, shave the cheese over the salad.  Serve immediately.

recipes.Ingredients:
1  red bell pepper, cut into  ½-inch (1-cm) squares
1  onion, chopped
4  cloves garlic, chopped
3 tbsp. (45 ml) vegetable oil
1 lb. (454 g) ground beef
¼ cup (60 ml) chili powder
2 tsp. (10 ml) ground coriander
1 tsp. (5 ml) ground cumin
1 tsp. (5 ml) ground ginger
1  pinch cayenne (optional)
3 tbsp. (45 ml) molasses
3 tbsp. (45 ml) ketchup
2 tbsp. (30 ml) Dijon mustard
2 tbsp. (30 ml) red wine vinegar
1 can (796 ml/28 oz) crushed tomatoes
1 can (540 ml/19 oz) red kidney beans
Salt and pepper
1 tbsp. (15 ml) whole-grain mustard
recipes.Procedure: 1. In a Dutch oven or large pot over medium heat, soften the bell pepper, onion and garlic in the oil.  Add the meat and brown. Add the spices and cook for 2 minutes.  Add the molasses and ketchup and cook for 2 minutes.  Add the Dijon mustard, vinegar, tomatoes and beans.  Lower the heat and simmer for 45 minutes.   Season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat and stir in the whole-grain mustard.

recipes.Ingredients: Red ripe Jalapeño, or Fresno peppers
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Remove stems from peppers, wash and slice in half lengthwise.
2.  Dry peppers in an oven on its lowest setting, or in a food dehydrator, until thoroughly dry.
3.  Cold-smoke peppers for 12-24 hours.
4.  Grind smoked peppers into powder.

recipes.Ingredients:
3  or more yellow onions
¼ cup unsalted butter
recipes.Procedure:
1.  Melt butter in a large saucepan.
2.  Add onions, stirring to coat with the butter.
3.  Cover and cook on low for at least 60 minutes, stirring occasionally.  If onions begin to scorch, add a small amount of water, and deglaze the pan, stirring the liquid into the onions.
4. When onions are a rich brown color, and approaching a liquid state, they are done.  They may be used immediately, stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, or frozen indefinitely.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup cranberries
½ cup unsalted butter
2 cups chopped celery
1  large onion, chopped
16 oz. French bread, cubed and dried
1 cup chopped pecans
4  Granny Smith apples - peeled, cored and chopped
½ cup unsalted butter, melted
2 cups chicken broth
4 tsp. chopped fresh sage
Turkey giblets, cooked and diced
salt and pepper to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large skillet, melt 1/2 cup butter over medium heat. Saute the celery and onion in the butter for 10 minutes. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.
2. In the same skillet, cook the giblets over medium-high heat until crumbled and evenly brown. Drain.
3. Combine the giblets and bread cubes with the celery and onion mixture. Stir in the cranberries, pecans, and apples. Mix in melted butter, chicken broth,  the stuffing should be totally moistened. Season with sage, salt, and pepper.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
1½ lbs.beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
½ tsp. salt, divided
6 tbsp. all-purpose flour, divided
½ tsp. smoked paprika or Chipotle powder
1 tbsp. canola oil
3 tbsp. tomato paste
2 tsp. herbes de Provence
2  garlic cloves, minced
2 cups dry red wine
2 cups beef broth
1½ tsp. minced fresh rosemary, divided
2  bay leaves
3 cups cubed peeled potatoes
3 cups coarsely chopped onions (about 2 large)
2 cups sliced carrots
2 tbsp. cold water
2 tbsp. balsamic or red wine vinegar
1 cup fresh or frozen peas
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a small bowl, toss beef with ¼ tsp. of salt. In a large bowl, combine 4 tbsp. of flour with the smoked paprika, then add a few pieces of beef in, turning until they’re lightly coated.
2. In a Dutch oven over medium heat, brown coated beef in oil until it starts to get some color
3. Next, stir in the tomato paste, herbes de Provence and garlic, stirring until they’ve darkened in color and have become fragrant. Pour in the wine and let the pot come to a slight boil, making sure to scrape up all the bits and pieces that have crusted to the bottom of the Dutch oven.
4. Once the wine has reduced by half, add the beef broth, 1 teaspoon. of rosemary and bay leaves, then let it all come to a boil. Cut the heat, cover and let the stew simmer until the meat is almost tender, about an hour and a half.
4.Add potatoes, onions and carrots, and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes, or until the veggies and meat are tender.
5. Pick out the bay leaves and discard them. Then, in a small bowl, mix the remaining rosemary, salt, flour, water and balsamic vinegar until it’s smooth. Pour the mixture into the stew, allow it to come to a boil and then add peas. After a few minutes, the stew should thicken and be ready to be served. Ladle into a bowl, pair with some crusty bread and dig in.

recipes.Author: Mrs. Major Huff
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup orange juice
¼ cup brown sugar (If you like it sweeter, you can double this.)
¼ cup regular sugar
¼ cup orange marmalade
½ tsp. cinnamon
¼ tsp. ginger
¼ tsp. allspice
12 oz. fresh cranberries, 1 bag in the produce or frozen section
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine the orange juice, both sugars, marmalade, cinnamon, ginger, allspice and the whole cranberries in a medium saucepan over medium heat and bring to a boil. 
2. Reduce to a gentle boil and stir for 10 minutes.
The berries will burst and will eventually break down to the sauce.
3. Let cool and then refrigerate. You can serve warm if you want to, but I like to chill for at least 2 hours.

recipes.Ingredients:
1  whole turkey, fresh or defrosted
1  whole onion, quarters and separated into pieces
2 tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp. rubbed sage
1 tbsp. garlic salt
1 tsp. freshly ground pepper
2 tsp. paprika
½ cup chicken stock
buttermilk
kosher or canning salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. The day before roasting, put the turkey into a buttermilk brine (mix enough buttermilk to cover turkey, with 1 tsp. kosher or canning salt per cup of buttermilk), and leave in the refrigerator overnight.
2. Place oven rack in lowest position. Preheat oven to 325°F. Place roasting rack in shallow roasting pan. Mix seasonings in small bowl.
3. In a plastic bag, mix the onion pieces and 1 tbsp. of the olive oil. Shake bag to coat onions with oil. Add 1 tbsp. of the spice mixture and shake bag again to coat with the spices.
4. Place turkey, breast-side up, in prepared pan. Stuff cavity with the spice-coated onions. Brush turkey breast with remaining olive oil. Spread remaining seasoning mixture over entire surface and under skin of turkey. Add ½ cup stock to pan. Cover turkey loosely with heavy duty foil.
5. Roast 1 hour. Remove foil. Roast 2 to 2 ½ hours longer or until internal temperature reaches 165°F (175°F in thigh), basting occasionally with pan juices. Remove turkey from oven. Let stand 20 minutes. Transfer to platter or carving board and slice. Reserve pan juices to make gravy or to serve with turkey.

recipes.RecipeName: Crispy Roast Duck With Cranberry Glaze
recipes.Ingredients:
1½ cups cranberries
½ cup honey
2 cups water
1  4-pound duck
1  3-inch strip of orange peel
1  medium onion
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
as desired
? cup white wine
½ cup sugar
1 tbsp. balsamic vinegar
Buttermilk brine
recipes.Procedure:
Step 1
Rinse the cranberries carefully under running water and pick them
over to remove any that have spoiled.
Step 2
Mix one cup of cranberries, the honey and one-half cup of water in a
small saucepan and cook, simmering, until the cranberries are very
soft. Strain through a sieve into a small bowl. The honey liquid is the
glaze for the duck.
Untruss your duck and lightly score the skin all over in a diamond pattern. Place upside down in a tight-fitting cooking pot and pour in as much cooled brine as is needed to cover the duck. Transfer to the fridge for at least 6 hours (but anything up to 24 hours), then place the pot on the heat, bring to a simmer and then cook for 10 minutes to just soften the skin.Step 3
Remove from the heat, then run under cold water to refresh and cool. Drain well, then pat the skin down with kitchen paper to remove as much moisture as possible. Season with a little salt and pepper. 
TipPreheat the oven to 140°C, fan 120°C, gas 1. Sit the duck on a wire rack, with a roasting tin below to catch the juices, and cook for 1 hour to dry the skin and cook the duck slowly and evenly.
Remove from the oven and leave to stand until cool, about 1 hour. Set your oven to the highest setting possible.
Now cook the duck (again on a rack, with a roasting tin below), until the skin crisps up – about 15 minutes. If you want a well-done duck, cook for another 30 minutes with the oven turned down to 180°C, fan 160°C, gas 4Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Remove the gizzard, heart and liver
from the duck and set aside. Put the orange peel, half the onion and
about half a tsp. of salt and pepper in the cavity. Paint the duck
with a little of the cranberry glaze.
Step 4
Place the duck on a rack in a roasting pan and roast for 45 minutes.
Every 15 minutes, paint the surface with a little of the cranberry glaze.
Remove the duck from the oven and prick the skin all over with a fork
to release the fat. Return to the oven and continue roasting, painting
every 15 minutes with the glaze, for a total of two hours.
Step 5
While the duck is roasting, make a broth with the innards: Roughly
chop the remaining half onion and the duck innards. Place in a small
saucepan with the wine, another half tsp. of salt and pepper and
a cup of water. Simmer gently for an hour or more, until the broth is
reduced to approximately one-half cup of flavorful liquid. Strain the
broth and discard the solids.
Step 6
Mix the remaining half cup of cranberries with the remaining half cup
of water, the sugar and the balsamic vinegar. Cook together for 10
minutes until the mixture is syrupy. Set aside

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1  14-oz. can tomatoes
2 cups chicken stock
1  potato, small diced
½  onion, chopped fine
1½ tsp. dried parsley flakes
1½ tsp. dried celery leaves
1  cod fillet, 4-6 oz., cut into 1" pieces
10  medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
white pepper
sea salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. Process the tomatoes lightly in blender until they become a thick, slighly chunky sauce. Mix with chicken stock in large saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat; reduce heat, cover and simmer for about 15 min.
2. Add onion, potato, parsely, and celery leaves, and simmer for about 30 min.
3. Add cod and shrimp. Simmer about 20 min., or until cod is just cooked, and shrimp are red. Add salt and white pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.Blurb: There is no definitive Stollen.  For cranberries and pecans, substitute an equal amount of any other dried or candied fruit or nuts.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tsp. active dry yeast
1 tbsp. warm water (110° to 115°)
½ cup warm 2% milk (110° to 115°)
3 tbsp. butter, softened
¼ cup sugar
1  large egg, lightly beaten
¾ tsp. grated lemon zest
¼ tsp. salt
2½ cups all-purpose flour
1 cup fresh or frozen cranberries
¼ cup chopped pecans
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water. Add the milk, butter, sugar, eggs, lemon zest, salt and 1 ½ cups flour. Add the cranberries and pecans. Add enough remaining flour to form a soft dough.
2. Turn onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. Place in a greased bowl, turning once to grease top. Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 ½ hours.
3. Punch dough down; cover and let rest for 10 minutes. Roll into a 12x7-in. oval. Fold a long side over to within 1 in. of opposite side; press edge lightly to seal. Place on greased baking sheet; curve ends slightly. Cover and let rise until nearly doubled, about 1 hour.
4. Bake at 375° for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown. Cool on wire rack. Spread with lemon-rum glaze.

recipes.Blurb: Freezing and then reheating the croissants is the secret to their perfect flakiness.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup water
3 tbsp. unsalted butter
3 cups bread flour
2 tbsp. dry milk
3 tbsp. sugar
¾ tsp. salt
3 tsp. active dry yeast
½ cup cold unsalted butter
1  egg white, slightly beaten
recipes.Procedure:
1. Add water, 3 tbsp. butter, flour, dry milk, sugar and salt to bread pan. Make a well in the center of the ingredients and add the yeast. Program for Dough. When finished, place dough into greased bowl. Cover and refrigerate 30 min.
2. Place dough on lightly floured surface. Roll into a 12x15 inch rectangle. Cover 2/3 of dough with thinly sliced butter. Fold unbuttered third of dough over the center buttered third, then fold again over the remaining buttered third. (Figure 1) Seal ends and long side of dough. Place on lightly greased baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 min.
3. Place dough on lightly floured surface. Roll into a 12x15 inch rectangle. Fold in thirds. (Figure 2) Place back onto greased baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
4. Place dough on lightly floured surface. Roll into a 12x15 inch rectangle. Cut rectangle into thirds, both crosswise and lengthwise, making 9 pieces. Cut each piece diagonally into two pieces.(Figure 3) Starting at the wide end, roll each piece into a rope, then place on baking sheet, shaping into a crescent shape. (Figure 4)
5. Cover and let rise until double in size. Brush with lightly beaten egg white.
6. Bake in preheated 375º oven for 13-15 minutes until lightly browned: The idea is to just slightly underbake them. Cool, then freeze thoroughly, and package until ready to serve. To serve, reheat croissants in 350º oven for ten minutes.

recipes.Blurb: This is an authentic Saxon recipe.
recipes.Ingredients:
500  g. raisins
100  g. currants
100  g. lemon peel
100  g. orange peel
250  g. chopped almonds,
16  g. vanilla sugar
6 tbsp. brown rum
12  drops of bitter almond oil
1 kg. of flour
2  cubes of yeast (84g)
150  g. of sugar
250  ml. milk
2  egg yolks
400  g. butter

Furthermore:
Flour for the countertop
150  g. butter
125  g. powdered sugar or fine sugar
recipes.Procedure:
1. Mix the raisins, currants, lemon peel, orange peel, almonds, vanilla sugar, rum and bitter almond oil and cover. Let stand for 6 hours. Stir every now and then.
2. Sift the flour into a large bowl. Press an indentation in the middle. Crumble in the yeast. Sprinkle with 1 tbsp. of sugar. Heat the milk to lukewarm, pour on it and mix with a little flour to make a pre-dough. Cover and let rise for about 15 minutes.
3. Add the remaining sugar, egg yolks and butter in pieces. First work through with the dough hook of the hand mixer, then knead with your hands to a smooth texture. Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes. 
4. Press the dough flat on a lightly floured work surface. Put the fruit on top, press into the dough and knead. Cover and let rise for another 30 minutes.
5. Knead the dough briefly. For a large stollen roll the dough into an oval 3-4cm thick plate. Press in the middle of the dough sheet lengthways and fold one half of the dough over the other. Or shape correspondingly small loaves.
6. Place the Stollen on a baking sheet lined with baking paper and let rise for another 15 minutes. Preheat the oven to 350 ° F.
7. Bake the Stollen in the preheated oven for 70-90 minutes on the lower rack. Heat the butter. Prick the stollen several times with a stick and brush with half of the melted butter while it is still warm. Dust with half of the powdered sugar, repeat the process after 5 minutes.
PLACE THE COOLED LOAVES IN AN AIR-TIGHT CONTAINER AND LEAVE 1 WEEK (BETTER 2 WEEKS) TO REST.

recipes.Author: Epicurious
recipes.Ingredients:
Peppers of your choice
Salt
Vinegar of your choice
recipes.Procedure:
1. Wash peppers; remove stems. Cut into small pieces and fine-chop in a food processor. Place in large bowl.
2. Add salt to 2% of the weight of the peppers and mix thoroughly.
3. Place mash in a glass container. Place a layer of plastic wrap directly on top of mash. Cover container and store at in a cool, dry place for two weeks. Bubbles will form in the liquid as it ferments.
4. Place mash in blender and add an equal quantity of vinegar. Process into liquid. Place in glass container and refrigerate for two more weeks. Strain, if desired, and bottle sauce.

recipes.Author: Taste Of Home
recipes.Ingredients:
6 lbs. cabbage (about 2 heads)
3 tbsp. canning salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. Quarter cabbages and remove cores; slice 1/8 in. thick. In an extra-large bowl, combine salt and cabbage. With clean hands, squeeze cabbage until it wilts and releases liquid, about 10 minutes. If desired, add optional ingredients.
2. Firmly pack cabbage mixture into 4-quart fermenting crock or large glass container, removing as many air bubbles as possible. If cabbage mixture is not covered by 1-2 inches of liquid, make enough brine to cover by 1-2 inches. To make brine, combine 4-1/2 tsp. canning salt per 1 quart of water in a saucepan; bring to a boil until salt is dissolved. Cool brine before adding to crock.
3. Place crock weight over cabbage; the weight should be submerged in the brine. Or, place an inverted dinner plate or glass pie plate over cabbage. The plate should be slightly smaller than the container opening, but large enough to cover most of the shredded cabbage mixture. Weigh down the plate with 2 or 3 sealed quart jars filled with water. If using a glass container with a lid, cover the opening loosely so any gas produced by the fermenting cabbage can escape. Alternately, you can cover the opening with a clean, heavy towel. If using a crock, seal according to manufacturer's instructions.
4. Store crock, undisturbed, at 70°-75° for 3-4 weeks (bubbles will form and aroma will change). Cabbage must be kept submerged below surface of the fermenting liquid throughout fermentation. Check crock 2-3 times each week; skim and remove any scum that may form on top of liquid. Fermentation is complete when bubbling stops. Transfer to individual containers. Cover and store in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.
TEST KITCHEN TIPS
Canning salt must be used. It does not contain additives like anti-caking agents that might be present in table or Kosher salt.
A fermenting vessel is worth the investment if you plan to make sauerkraut frequently; particularly because of the included weight and the water seal features. The water seal allows gasses to escape but prevents other contaminates from entering.

recipes.Author: Feastingathome.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
2 lbs. napa cabbage, cored and cut into 1-inch pieces (one large cabbage)
¼ cup sea salt
2 cups daikon radish, cut into matchstick strips (optional, or use carrots)
1  bunch scallions, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp. fresh ginger, sliced ( 2-3 disks, peels ok)
6  cloves garlic, whole
1  shallot, quartered (optional)
2 tbsp. Korean-style red pepper flakes (gochugaru)
2 tbsp. fish sauce ( or use vegan fish sauce, miso paste, or soy sauce), more to taste
2 tsp. sugar ( or an alternative like honey, brown rice syrup)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Cut the Napa cabbage into 1-inch cubes.Place napa cabbage in a bowl and toss with ¼ cup sea salt.Fill the bowl with filtered water and stir, and soak cabbage for 6-8 hours.Place plate over the napa cabbage to keep it submerged.After 6- 8 hours, drain (making sure to save the brine) and rinse lightly, pressing the liquid out. Replace in bowl; add radish and scallions.
2. Meanwhile, In a food processor, make a paste with the garlic, ginger, shallot, Korean chili flakes (or Gochujang) and optional fish sauce (or miso) and sugar. Peel and cut the daikon radish (or carrot) into match sticks, about 2-3 inches longCut the scallions into 1-2 inch pieces.
3. Place the drained cabbage along with the daikon, scallions and chili paste into the bowl. Massage a bit with gloved hands. Pack tightly into fermenting crock. Pour a little of the brine into the jar, just to enough to cover the cabbage. Place fermentation weight over cabbage, cover and place in a cool, dark place for 3-5 days.
4. After 3 days, tap the jar to see if any bubbles rise to the top- indicating that it is fermenting .If no action, give it another day or two. If you don’t see bubbles when tapping the jar, it just may need a couple more days- especially in cooler climates. Taste the kimchi for tanginess. Continue to ferment for 2-3 more days if you want it tangier or softer
5. Pack in bottles, making sure Kimchi stays below brine, and refrigerate for 2 weeks.The longer you ferment, the more complex and tangy the taste. If you like a fizzy brine, tighten the lid, burping every week or so. If you don’t want to think about it, give the lid one loose twist, so it’s on there, but gases can escape. 
Keep fermented kimchi in a 2-quart jar or crock with the lid on, pressing it down under the brine after each use.
It will keep for months on end in the fridge when the kimchi is submerged below the brine….getting better and more flavorful with time!
If you need or want to add more salt brine to the kimchi, to keep it submerged, mix water and salt at this ratio: 1 cup water and 1 ¼ tsp. fine sea salt. Stir it together first, pour over the kimchi.

recipes.Author: Allrecipes.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
½  gallon spring or distilled water
2  lbs.cucumbers
1 cup spring or distilled water
⅓ cup canning salt
5  cloves fresh garlic, or more to taste
1  bunch fresh dill, stems trimmed
3  dried chile de arbol peppers (Optional)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Crisp cucumbers by storing in the refrigerator or soaking in very cold water for 1 hour.
2. Bring 1 cup water to a boil in a saucepan. Add salt and stir to combine. Set aside to cool.
3. Wash cucumbers in cold water and remove any blossoms that may be clinging to them. Quarter large cucumbers lengthwise. Cut medium cucumbers in half lengthwise. Leave gherkin-sized cucumbers whole.
4. Peel and gently crush garlic cloves, but don't splinter them into fragments.
5. Pour cooled salt water into a ½-gallon Mason jar. Add cucumbers, garlic, dill, and dried chile peppers, arranged attractively. Pack cucumbers tightly; they will shrink as they pickle. Fill the jar with remaining water until cucumbers are just covered to avoid overly diluting the brine.
6. Loosely cover the jar and set aside at room temperature. Set the jar on a dish if it is very full, to catch any dribbles. Give the pickles 12 to 24 hours to begin fermenting. Refrigerate them, in brine and loosely covered, as they approach the stage of pickling you prefer: new, half-sour, or sour. Don't overshoot the mark, as refrigeration slows, but does not stop, fermentation.

recipes.Author: Food.Com
recipes.Ingredients:
oil, as needed
1 tsp. minced garlic
2 cups chopped tomatoes
salt and pepper
1 cup mixed good olive
8  -12 slices veal, thin slices
flour, for dredging
1  lemon, thinly sliced
chopped fresh parsley leaves (to garnish)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Heat oven to 200°.
2. Put 2 tbsp. olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat; add garlic and, when it sizzles, add tomatoes, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down, about 10 minutes, then add olives, and turn heat to low.
3. Put about 3 tbsp. olive oil in a large skillet, preferably nonstick, over medium-high heat.
Sprinkle veal with salt and pepper, then dredge it in flour. Sauté as many slices as will comfortably fit in skillet, just until brown on both sides, 5 minutes or less. Remove to a plate, and keep warm in oven while sautéing remaining slices.
4. Taste sauce, and adjust seasoning; spoon it over veal slices, and arrange lemon on top. Sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

recipes.Blurb: This is a pork-based version of souvlaki, instead of lamb.
recipes.Author: realgreekrecipes.com
recipes.Ingredients:
700  g. boneless pork neck
1  lemon, juiced
3 tbsp. olive oil
1 tsp. dried oregano, plus extra for garnish
salt and pepper
For the dressing:
1  lemon, juiced
olive oil
recipes.Procedure:
1. Cut the meat into small pieces, about 2 cm. x 2 cm. x 1 cm. thick. Thread onto wooden skewers and place in baking pan.
2. Mix lemon juice, olive oil, oregan and a bit of pepper and mix well. Pour over skewers; turn to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours, or up to overnight.
3. Grill meat for 10-15 min., turning occasionally.
4. For the dressing (Ladolemono):
In a bottle that you can shake, add lemon juice and 2/3 of that quantity of juice in olive oil. Shake container until a creamy dressing forms, and pour over souvlaki right as they come off the grill. Serve with a sprinkle of oregano on top.

recipes.Author: NY Times
recipes.Ingredients:
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
several sprigs thyme
1 tbsp. garlic, minced
1 cup sun-dried tomatoes, roughly chopped
2 tbsp. capers, drained
½ cup dry white wine
16  large shrimp, peeled
salt and pepper
fresh basil, chopped.
recipes.Procedure:
1. Put oil in large skillet over medium heat and add thyme, garlic, tomatoes and capers. Cook just until mixture sizzles, then add wiine; raise heat and bring to a boil. Cook for about 1 min., then add shrimp, turning them in sauce.
2. Continue cooking shrimp until done, 3-5 min., turning once. Sprinkle with salt and pepper; garnish with basil. Serve hot or warm.

recipes.Author: geniuskitchen.com
recipes.Ingredients:
1  medium zucchini
1 tbsp. butter
1  clover garlic, minced
2 tbsp. sun-dried tomatoes, coarsely chopped.
¼ tsp. salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. Cut zucchini into ½" slices, then cut each slice into quarters (you should have about 2 cups).
2. Melt butter in nonstick pan and add zucchini. Sauté, stirring often, about 3 min.
3. Add garlic and sauté about 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and continue to sauté, stirring often, for about 2 more minutes.
5. Toss with salt and serve.

recipes.Author: tasteofhome.com
recipes.Ingredients:
1  package (1 pound) spaghetti or linguine
6  strips pancetta or bacon, chopped
1 cup fresh or frozen peas
2 tbsp. lemon juice
1½ tsp. grated lemon zest
2  large eggs, lightly beaten
2 tbsp. minced fresh parsley
½ cup grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
¼ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. pepper
Additional grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, optional
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a large saucepan, cook pasta according to package directions for al dente. Drain pasta, reserving pasta water; keep pasta warm. In same pot, cook bacon over medium heat until crisp, stirring occasionally. Add peas; cook until just heated through.
2. Add pasta to pot; toss to combine. Stir in remaining ingredients, adding enough reserved pasta water for sauce to reach desired consistency. If desired, serve with additional cheese.

recipes.Author: Bon Appétit
recipes.Ingredients:
3  quarts whole milk (avoid ultra-pasteurized)
¼ cup white vinegar or lemon juice.
½ tsp. kosher salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. Pour milk, vinegar and salt into a saucepan over medium heat. Use lemon juice or a different vinegar to give the cheese different flavors.
2. Bring the mixture to the absolute barest simmer you can, adjusting the heat as necessary—the mixture should be steaming, but not bubbling. If you have a thermometer, 180–185° is the sweet spot but 10° in either direction will still net you some tasty cheese.
3. Simmer 25 minutes without stirring.
4. Remove from heat, and remove curds with slotted spoon, placing them in a colander lined with cheesecloth. Allow to drain for about 10-30 minutes: less time yields softer curds. Makes about 1 lb. ricotta.
