1. Heat saucepan to medium high. Add 1 tbsp. unsalted butter to pan. When melted, add shallot and cook until transparent. Add white wine, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, pepper, sugar to the pan. Bring to simmer (still on medium high) and reduce by half (~3 minutes).
2. Add cream, simmer for 2 minutes.
3. Turn heat to low and add cold butter one cube at a time while mixing with wooden spoon. Once all the butter is incorporated, the sauce should be thickened, satiny and beautifully glossy.

recipes.Ingredients:
2 tsp. Dried Sage
1½ tsp. Dried Thyme
1 tsp. Dried Marjoram
¾ tsp. Dried Rosemary
½ tsp. Ground Nutmeg
½ tsp. Black Pepper
recipes.Procedure: Mix ingredients in mortar or spice grinder. Process into powder. Store in airtight container.

recipes.Blurb: Known as Bûche de Noël, this cake is traditional at Christmas time.
recipes.Author: lifeloveandsugar.com
recipes.Ingredients:
¾ cup Cake Flour
⅓ cup Hershey's Special Dark Cocoa Powder
1 tsp. Baking Powder
0.62 tsp. Salt
4 large Eggs (divided)
¾ cup Granulated Sugar
5 tbsp. Sour Cream
¼ cup Butter (melted)
2 tsp. Vanilla Extract
1¼ cups Heavy Whipping Cream (cold)
¾ cups Powdered Sugar
8 ounces Mascarpone Cheese (softened but still chilled)
8 ounces Semi Sweet Chocolate (finely chopped)
1 cup Heavy Whipping Cream
add Sugared Cranberries (optional)
add Sugared Rosemary (optional)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 17×12 inch jelly roll sheet pan with parchment paper. Make sure the parchment paper sticks up at least an inch above the sides of the pan on all sides. You’ll use the parchment paper later to lift the cake out of the pan and roll it up.
2. Whisk the flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt together in a medium bowl and set aside.
3. In a large bowl, combine the egg yolks and sugar and whisk together until well combined.
4. Add the sour cream, melted butter and vanilla extract and whisk together until well combined.
5. Add the dry ingredient mixture (previously set aside) to the wet ingredient mixture and gently whisk together until well combined, then set aside.
6. Add the egg whites to a large mixer bowl and whip on high speed until stiff peaks form.
7. Gently fold about 1/3 of the whipped egg whites into the chocolate mixture to loosen up the batter.
8. Add the remaining egg whites and gently fold together until well combined.
9. Spread the cake batter evenly into the prepared pan and bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the top of the cake springs back when toughed and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
10. Remove the cake from the oven and immediately lift the cake out of the pan using the parchment paper and place it on the counter.
11. While the cake is hot, use the parchment paper the cake was baked in and start at the shorter end of the cake to slowly roll the cake up. Set the cake aside to cool completely.
12. When the cake has cooled and is ready to be filled, make the filling. Add the heavy whipping cream, powdered sugar, vanilla extract and salt to a large mixer bowl and whip on high speed until soft peaks form.
13. Add the mascarpone cheese to the whipped cream and whip until stiff peaks form. It will happen fairly quickly.
14. Unroll the cake roll very carefully, looking out for areas where it may be sticking to release it. You can use an offset spatula or something similar and run it along the parchment paper as you unroll the cake to help release it as it unrolls.
15. Spread the filling evenly onto the unrolled cake, then roll it back up without the parchment paper.
16. Wrap it up in plastic wrap with the seam side down and refrigerate for at least an hour to firm up.
17. When you’re read to decorate the cake, make the chocolate ganache. Add the chocolate to a medium sized bowl and set aside. Heat the cream in the microwave just until it begins to boil, then pour it over the chocolate.
18. Allow the chocolate and cream to sit for a few minutes, then whisk until smooth. Let the ganache cool to about room temperature (or cooler, you don’t want it too warm/thin), then transfer to a large mixer bowl.
19. Whip on high speed until lightened in color and thick enough to spread.
20. To decorate the cake, use a large serrated knife to gently cut off a piece of the log about 3 inches in length. Make the cut with a slight diagonal.
21. Use some of the chocolate ganache to attach the small log to the side of the larger log.
22. Spread the remaining chocolate ganache all over the cake, then use a fork to create bark-like lines all over it. Decorate with sugared cranberries and rosemary if desired.
23. Refrigerate the cake until ready to serve.

recipes.Blurb: Use these to add a festive touch to Holiday desserts.
recipes.Author: lifeloveandsugar.com
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup granulated sugar, divided
½ cup water
cranberries
fresh rosemary sprigs
recipes.Procedure:
1. Bring ½ cup of sugar and ½ cup of water to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes, until sugar has melted.
2. Remove from heat and let cool for about 10 minutes. 
3.Spread ½ cup of sugar evenly on a shallow dish. Dip cranberries and rosemary springs into the sugar water, then roll in the sugar. Let dry before adding to your dessert. You can also use some of the clumps of sugar left behind to add “snow” to the dessert.

recipes.RecipeName: Fall-Apart Roasted Pork Shoulder with Rosemary, Mu
recipes.Author: Katie Workman
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. chopped garlic
2  anchovies (rinsed)
1 tbsp. chopped fresh rosemary
1 tsp. kosher salt
½ tsp. freshly ground pepper
2 tbsp. olive oil
1 tbsp. coarse Dijon mustard
1  (3-pound) boneless pork shoulder (trimmed of excess fat and tied)
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a small food processor, combine the garlic, anchovies, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Add the olive oil and process until it forms a paste, scraping down the sides. Remove the blade and use a fork or spoon to stir in the mustard. Rub the paste all over the pork shoulder, loosely cover it with plastic wrap, and refrigerate from 2 to 24 hours.
2. Preheat the oven to 450° F and bring the pork to room temperature while the oven heats. Place the pork in a shallow roasting pan and roast, uncovered, for 20 minutes, until the top starts to brown a bit.
3. Turn the heat down to 250° F and continue to cook, uncovered, for 4 to 5 hours until the middle of the roast registers 180° F on an internal thermometer, and as you slide the thermometer in you can feel that the meat is very tender throughout. If juices are in the pan (and I have found that sometimes there are and sometimes none), pour off the juices from the pan into a heatproof container, like a Pyrex measuring cup. Place this in the fridge, where the fat will rise to the top, while the meat rests.
4. When the meat is cooked, if you think that the outside of the roast could use a bit more crust/brownness, turn the heat back up to 450° F and let it cook for another 15 to 20 minutes to give the outside a bit more of a crunchy texture.
5. Remove from the oven and let sit for about 20 minutes. Spoon the fat off the reserved juices in the fridge and pour the cooking juices into a serving pitcher or bowl (warm it a bit in the microwave or in a small pot if you like). Slice the pork as thinly or thickly as you like, knowing the meat will fall apart at least slightly. Sprinkle the sliced meat with a bit of salt before serving, and pass the pan juices on the side to drizzle over.

recipes.Ingredients:
1 lb. yellow baby new potatoes, halved
2  (12-oz) jars marinated quartered artichoke hearts, drained and patted dry
¼ cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
2½ tbsp. olive oil
1 tsp. smoked paprika
1 tsp. kosher salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. Mix olive oil, paprika and salt. Add to a plastic bag with potatoes and toss until potatoes are well-coated.
2. Add artichokes to bag and toss to mix.
3. Spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment. Bake in a preheated 350º oven for 45-60 minutes, or until potatoes are nicely browned and artichokes lightly charred.
4. Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.

recipes.Author: allrecipes.com
recipes.Ingredients:
2½ lbs. beef tenderloin
4 tbsp. butter, softened, divided
2 tbsp. butter
1  onion, chopped
½ cup sliced fresh mushrooms
2  ounces liver paté
salt and pepper to taste
1  (17.5 ounce) package frozen puff pastry, thawed
1  large egg yolk, beaten
1  (10.5 ounce) can beef broth
2 tbsp. red wine
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat the oven to 425° F (220°C).
2. Place beef tenderloin in a baking dish. Spread 2 tbsp. softened butter over beef.
3.Bake in the preheated oven until browned, 10 to 15 minutes. Remove beef from the pan and reserve pan juices; allow beef to cool completely.
4. Increase oven temperature to 450° F (230° C).
5. Melt 2 tbsp. butter in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté onion and mushrooms in butter for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.
6. Mix paté and remaining 2 tbsp. softened butter together in a bowl; season with salt and pepper. Spread paté mixture over beef. Top with onion and mushroom mixture.
7. Roll out puff pastry dough to about 1/4-inch thickness and place beef in the center.
8. Fold up and seal all the edges, making sure the seams are not too thick. Place beef in a 9x13-inch baking dish, cut a few slits in the top of dough, and brush with egg yolk.
9. Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 425° F (220° C) and continue baking until pastry is a rich, golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read between 122° to 130° F (50° to 54°C) for medium rare. Set aside to rest.
10. Meanwhile, place reserved pan juices in a small saucepan over high heat. Stir in beef broth and red wine; boil until slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Strain and serve with beef. Serve hot and enjoy!

recipes.Author: Adapted by Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
2 lbs. Russet Potatoes, washed and cut into 1 inch cubes
½ cup plus 3 tbsp. olive oil, divided
½ tsp. smoked paprika
½ tsp. garlic powder
½ tsp. onion powder
½ tsp. Kosher salt
½ tsp. black pepper
1 tsp. dried parsley

fresh thyme leaves, optional
recipes.Procedure:
1. Scrub potatoes well. Cut potatoes into 1 inch cubes.
2. Place in a pan and cover with cold water. Place on the stove on a high heat and bring to the boil, then turn down the heat and simmer for 8-9 minutes – until softened at the edges.
3. Drain the potatoes in a colander, and give them a good shake to really roughen up the edges. Don't worry if a few break apart and they look overly fluffy. The more fluffy they are, the better they'll absorb the fat and the crispier they'll be.
4. Preheat oven to 425°F. Add ½ olive oil to baking pan and place in oven until oil is shimmering.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tbsp. olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, Kosher salt, black pepper, and dried parsley.
6. Drizzle the olive oil mixture over the potatoes. Gently mix the potatoes to ensure they are all covered with the seasoning.
7. Carefully place the potatoes – using tongs – in the baking tin with the hot fat, then place them in the oven.
8. Cook for 30-35 minutes, turning once or twice in the last 15 minutes of cooking, until golden brown and crispy. If desired, sprinkle with fresh thyme leaves before serving.

recipes.RecipeName: Roasted Broccoli and Garlic with Lemon and Parmesa
recipes.Ingredients:
4 lbs. broccoli
4  garlic cloves peeled and sliced
5 tbsp. olive oil
1½ tsp. kosher salt
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
2 tsp. grated lemon zest
2 tbsp. freshly squeezed lemon juice
⅓ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F
2. Wash and dry the broccoli (if not dry, it will not brown well). Cut the broccoli florets from the thick stalks, leaving an inch or two of stalk attached to the florets, discarding the rest of the stalks. Cut the larger pieces through the base of the head with a small knife, pulling the florets apart. You should have about 8 cups of florets.
3. Place the broccoli florets on a sheet pan large enough to hold them in a single layer. Drizzle broccoli with 5 tbsp. olive oil. Sprinkle with the salt and pepper. 
4. Coat garlic with a bit of olive oil and set aside.
5. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until crisp-tender and the tips of some of the florets are browned. Add garlic during last 10 minutes of roasting.
6. Remove the broccoli from the oven and immediately toss with 1½ tbsp. olive oil, the lemon zest, lemon juice, and Parmesan. Serve hot.

recipes.Ingredients:
4 tbsp. beef drippings
4 tbsp. red wine
2 cups low-sodium beef broth
1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce
salt to taste
pepper to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place medium saucepan on stovetop over high heat. When saucepan is warm, add 4 tbsp. beef drippings, 4 tbsp. red wine, 2 cups low-sodium beef broth, and 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce.
2. Whisk ingredients together until incorporated, then bring mixture to boil. Once mixture begins to boil, reduce heat under saucepan to medium-low. Simmer mixture 5 minutes.
3. After 5 minutes, taste mixture and add salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste. When satisfied with flavor, transfer jus into serving container. Note: if your drippings contained any remnants from the beef, strain the jus through a fine mesh sieve first, so you're left with a smooth liquid.
4. Serve warm with prime rib, French dip sandwiches, roast beef, or other meal as desired.

recipes.Ingredients:
4 large potatoes preferably Russet, sliced into 2 ¼ x 3/ 8 in. strips (a mandolin makes this really easy)
1 cup all-purpose flour
½ cup cornstarch.
1 tsp. baking powder
1 tsp. salt
½ tsp. ground black pepper
¼ tsp. onion powder
1 bottle beer your favorite ale, stout or lager
1 large egg lightly beaten
8 pieces cod
Vegetable oil for frying
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place the potatoes in a bowl of ice water for about 30 minutes.
2. Heat the oil in a deep heavy skillet, or deep fryer to 330° F.
3. Drain the potatoes and dry them well with a kitchen towel.
4. Carefully, drop the potatoes, about 1 cup at a time, into the hot oil and fry for abut 3 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Repeat until all potatoes have gone through the 1st round of frying.
5. Increase the oil temperature to 365°F to 370°F.
6. Meanwhile, in a large bowl, stir together the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least an hour.  Next, add in the egg and beer. Stir to mix.
7. Add a little more flour on a platter and dredge the fish fillets.
8. Add the floured fillet to the batter and let the excess batter drip off.
9.Carefully add the fish to the hot oil. Cook until the fish is golden. Drain on paper towels.
10. To finish the chips, fry the pre-cooked potatoes in the hot oil. Fry until they are golden brown, and crisp, about 4 more minutes. Drain on paper towels.

recipes.Author: foodnetwork.com
recipes.Ingredients:
2  lbs.beef bottom round, trimmed of excess fat
2 tsp. kosher salt
1 tsp. freshly ground black pepper
¾ cup all-purpose flour
¼ cup vegetable oil or bacon drippings
1  large onion, thinly sliced
2  cloves garlic, minced
2  stalks celery, chopped
1 tbsp. tomato paste
1  (14.5-ounce) can diced tomatoes
1 tsp. smoked paprika
1 tsp. dried oregano
1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce
1½ cups beef broth
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat the oven to 325° F.
2. Cut the meat with the grain into 1/2-inch thick slices and season on both sides with the salt and pepper. Place the flour into a pie pan. Dredge the pieces of meat on both sides in the flour mixture. Tenderize the meat using a needling device, until each slice is 1/4-inch thick. Dredge the slices on both sides once more and set aside.
3. Add enough of the bacon drippings or vegetable oil to just cover the bottom of a 4 to 5-quart Dutch oven set over medium-high heat. Once the oil begins to shimmer, add the steaks to the pan, being careful not to overcrowd. Cook until golden brown on both sides, approximately 2 minutes per side. Remove the steaks to a plate and repeat until all of the steaks have been browned.
4.Remove the last steaks from the pot and add the onions, garlic, and celery. Saute for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomato paste and stir to combine. Next add the tomatoes, paprika, oregano, Worcestershire sauce and beef broth and stir to combine. Return the meat to the pot, submerging it in the liquid. Cover the pot and place it in the oven on the middle rack. Cook for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until the meat is tender and falling apart.

recipes.Author: spendwithpennies.com
recipes.Ingredients:
3 tbsp. butter divided
1½ lbs. boneless skinless chicken breasts cut into 1" pieces
4 tsp. Cajun seasoning divided
½ tsp. salt divided
½ tsp. black pepper divided
½  yellow onion diced
1  red bell pepper sliced
1  green bell pepper sliced
1½ cups heavy whipping cream
¾ tsp. smoked paprika
½ tsp. dried basil
¼ tsp. garlic powder
⅓ cup shredded Parmesan cheese
recipes.Procedure:
1. Place 2 tbsp. of butter in a large pan over medium-high heat until melted.
2. Meanwhile, combine 3 tsp. Cajun seasoning, ¼ tsp. salt, and ¼ tsp. pepper in a zippered bag. Add chopped chicken, zip closed, and shake until chicken is coated.
3. Transfer chicken to heated pan and cook until chicken is browned and just cooked through. Remove to a plate and set aside.
4. Add the remaining tbsp. of butter to pan and allow it to melt.
5. Add peppers and onion and cook until beginning to soften (about 3-5 minutes).
6. Add heavy cream, smoked paprika, basil, garlic powder, 1 tsp. cajun seasoning, and remaining ¼ tsp. salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and then reduce to a simmer, cooking until sauce is thickened.
7. Add parmesan cheese and stir until melted. Return cooked chicken and add cooked pasta, stir well and serve.

recipes.Ingredients:
16  ounces Rotini (or other medium pasta)
1  pint Grape Tomatoes (halved)
1  Bell Pepper (red or orange, diced)
½ cup Olives (sliced pitted)
½ cup Feta Cheese (crumbled)
⅓ cup Red Onion (diced)
For dressing:
2 tbsp. Greek Seasoning
¼ cup Red Wine Vinegar
⅓ cup Olive Oil
add Salt And Pepper
recipes.Procedure:
1. Whisk together dressing ingredients.
2. Cook pasta al dente according to package directions. 
3. Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Add dressing and toss.
4. Refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving

recipes.Ingredients:
¼ cup soy sauce
2 tbsp. peanut butter
1 tbsp. honey
20  drops Chinese hot sauce
2 tsp. white vinegar
2 tsp. sesame oil
⅛ tsp. garlic powder
⅛ tsp. ground black pepper
recipes.Procedure: Mix ingredients in small bowl with whisk. Refrigerate for up to 18 months.

recipes.Ingredients:
6 tbsp. hoisin sauce
2 tbsp. rice vinegar (not seasoned)
1 tbsp. Asian fish sauce
1 tbsp. soy sauce
1 tbsp. honey
⅓ cup minced shallot
2  garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp. minced peeled fresh ginger
⅛ tsp. Chinese five-spice powder
⅓ cup sugar
recipes.Procedure:
1. Stir together all ingredients except sugar in a bowl.
2. Cook sugar in a dry heavy saucepan over moderate heat, undisturbed, until it begins to melt. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally with a fork, until sugar is melted into a deep golden caramel. Tilt pan and carefully pour in hoisin mixture (caramel will harden and steam vigorously). Cook over moderately low heat, stirring, until caramel is dissolved and sauce is thickened, 6 to 8 minutes. Cool to room temperature. Serve with shrimp, swordfish, pork, or chicken

recipes.Ingredients:
3 cups Onions, diced
6 cups ( two bottles) of Passata.
3  cloves Garlic, diced
3 tbsp. olive oil
½ cups Cane Sugar
1 cup apple cider vinegar
some salt
1 tsp. Ginger
1 tsp. Curry Powder
1 tbsp. Mustard Seeds
2  Star Anise
½ tsp. cinnamon
1 tsp. Allspice
1 tsp. Ground Black Pepper
1  Chili (optional)
1 cans of Tomato Paste
2 tsp. Ground Curry
2 tsp. lemon juice
4 tbsp. Worcestershire Sauce
3 cups Red Onions, diced
4  lbs.fresh Tomatoes, peeled and diced or 3 cans of diced tomatoes
3  cloves Garlic, diced
3 tbsp. olive oil
½ cups Cane Sugar
250  ml (1 cup) apple cider vinegar
some salt
1 tsp. Ginger
1 tsp. Ground Curry
1 tbsp. Mustard Seeds
2  Star Anise
½ tsp. cinnamon
1 tsp. Allspice
1 tsp. Ground Black Pepper
1  Chili (optional)
1 cans of Tomato Paste
2 tsp. Ground Curry
2 tsp. lemon juice
4 tbsp. Worcestershire Sauce
15  Bratwurst
recipes.Procedure:
1. If the bratwursts are not pre-cooked, poach them in lightly simmering water first.
2. Grill or pan-fry them until they develop a crispy browned crust. (Some vendors cut vertical slits along the sausages before cooking to prevent bursting.)
3.Heat the oil in a large pot.
4. Add the Onions and saute until they are soft.
5. Add the Garlic and saute for a minute.
6. Add the Sugar and cook while stirring until the onions are caramelized.
7. Pour the Apple Cider Vinegar over it. Add the tomatoes or the cans of diced tomatoes.
8. Bring it back to a boil while you measure and mix the spices.
9. Mix all dry spices, but only 1 tsp. of curry into a small container, then mix it into the sauce. Let cook at medium heat for at least 30 minutes, better 60 minutes. Stir occasionally.
10. Put a fine mash sieve over an pot.
11. Push the tomato mass from the first pot through the sieve into the other pot. Keep the fluid to make the sauce.
Add the first can of Tomato Paste to the sauce and stir.
Bring the sauce back to a boil, if after some minutes of boiling the sauce is still too liquid, add more tomato paste. You want to reach the consistency of ketchup.
12.Now add the Curry, some Lemon Juice and the Worcestershire Sauce, also add salt to a taste.
13. For the bratwursts, grill or pan-fry 4 German bratwursts until browned and crispy, slice into bite-sized pieces, top with curry ketchup, sprinkle with curry powder, and serve with bread rolls or French fries.

recipes.Ingredients:
¼ cup coriander seeds
4 tsp. cumin seeds
1 tbsp. fennel seeds
1 tsp. fenugreek seeds
1 tsp. black peppercorns
1 tsp. yellow mustard seeds (optional, for added heat)
4  dried curry leaves (can substitute 1 large bay leaf)
2 tbsp. ground turmeric
½ tsp. ground ginger
½ tsp. garlic powder
½ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. ground cinnamon
recipes.Procedure:
Heat a skillet over medium heat and roast the whole spices and curry/bay leaves for a few minutes until very fragrant. Be careful not to scorch the spices or they will be bitter. Let the spices cool completely. Place the whole spices in a spice/coffee grinder along with the remaining ingredients and grind until you get a fine powder.
Store in an airtight jar in a dark, cool place. Will keep for several months but for best flavor use within a few weeks.

recipes.Ingredients:
1 cups Onions, diced
2 cups Passata.
1  cloves Garlic, diced
1 tbsp. olive oil
23⅔ tbsp. Cane Sugar
⅓ cup apple cider vinegar
some salt
⅓ tsp. Ginger
⅓ tsp. Curry Powder
1 tsp. Mustard Seeds
⅔ tsp. fennel seed
⅛ tsp. cinnamon
⅜  (tsp. Allspice
⅜ tsp. Ground Black Pepper
1  Chili (optional)
Tomato Paste, as needed
¾ tsp. Ground Curry
¾  lemon juice
4 tsp. Worcestershire Sauce
5  Bratwurst
recipes.Procedure:
1. If the bratwursts are not pre-cooked, poach them in lightly simmering water first.
2. Grill or pan-fry them until they develop a crispy browned crust. (Some vendors cut vertical slits along the sausages before cooking to prevent bursting.)
3.Heat the oil in a large pot.
4. Add the Onions and saute until they are soft.
5. Add the Garlic and saute for a minute.
6. Add the Sugar and cook while stirring until the onions are caramelized.
7. Pour the Apple Cider Vinegar over it. Add the tomatoes or the cans of diced tomatoes.
8. Bring it back to a boil while you measure and mix the spices.
9. Mix all dry spices, but only 1 tsp. of curry into a small container, then mix it into the sauce. Let cook at medium heat for at least 30 minutes, better 60 minutes. Stir occasionally.
10. Put a fine mash sieve over an pot.
11. Push the tomato mass from the first pot through the sieve into the other pot. Keep the fluid to make the sauce.
Add the first can of Tomato Paste to the sauce and stir.
Bring the sauce back to a boil, if after some minutes of boiling the sauce is still too liquid, add more tomato paste. You want to reach the consistency of ketchup.
12.Now add the Curry, some Lemon Juice and the Worcestershire Sauce, also add salt to a taste.
13. For the bratwursts, grill or pan-fry 4 German bratwursts until browned and crispy, slice into bite-sized pieces, top with curry ketchup, sprinkle with curry powder, and serve with bread rolls or French fries.

recipes.Ingredients:
500  g. bread flour
400  ml. water (80% hydration)
10  g. salt
2  g. instant yeast or 100 g. ripe sourdough starter
25  g. olive oil (plus more for topping)
Fresh rosemary, roughly chopped
Flaky sea salt
Optional: thinly sliced red onion, cherry tomatoes, or olives
recipes.Procedure:
1. Mix & Rest: Combine flour and water; let autolyse 30 minutes. Add yeast/starter, salt, and oil.
Stretch & Fold: Over 2–3 hours, perform 3–4 folds.
2. Bulk Ferment: Until doubled and bubbling—shorter for yeast, longer for sourdough.
Cold Proof (optional): Refrigerate overnight for flavor.
3. Pan & Dimple: Oil a pan generously, stretch dough gently. Press with fingers like your mother probably did—little dimples to hold love (and olive oil).
4. Top & Bake: Sprinkle rosemary, flaky salt, and maybe a whisper of garlic oil. Bake at 450°F until golden and audibly crisp.

recipes.Blurb: A velvety, fire-kissed sauce with pineapple brightness and deep, balanced heat.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with MS Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
2 cups passata (smooth tomato purée)
8 oz. pineapple fresh or canned, pureéd
a handful of cranberries, to taste
3  dried apricots, or to taste
½ cup brown sugar
¼ cup apple cider vinegar
2 tsp. Worcestershire sauce
Custom hot pepper blend, to taste (blended smooth)
1 tsp. smoked paprika
⅛ tsp. cardomon
⅛ tsp. ground allspice or clove (optional)
1 tbsp. blackstrap molasses (optional)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Purée fruit with hot peppers and cardomon until smooth. 
 Combine with other ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat.
2. Simmer gently for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
3. Blend again if needed for ultra-smooth texture.
4. Taste and adjust: more vinegar for brightness, more sugar for balance, more heat if desired.
5. Cool, bottle, and let rest several hours or overnight to allow flavors to meld.

Notes:
Sauce should be smooth and pourable; adjust consistency with a splash of water or more passata if needed.
Keeps well refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
Excellent on ribs, grilled chicken, or as a glaze for roasted vegetables.

recipes.Blurb:
This recipe was born during a thunderstorm when the smoker had to yield to the oven. The result? A deeper, richer rib with layers of smoke, fruit, and fire.
“Spareribs Donnerstürme” honors the improvisation of the moment and the power of a well-timed sto
recipes.Ingredients:
2  lbs.pork spareribs
Salt (Redmond or Himalayan preferred)
Freshly ground black pepper
¾ cup dry red wine
¾ cup water
2 tbsp. boiled cider
2  small habanero chiles (optional, for pre-smoke rub or sauce)
1  bay leaf
2  garlic cloves, smashed
recipes.Procedure:
1. Remove the membrane from the bone side of the ribs. Use a butter knife to lift a corner, then grip with a paper towel and peel away. Season generously with salt and pepper. Let sit at room temperature while preparing the smoker.
2. Smoke(Optional but Glorious)
 Preheat smoker to 225–250°F. Use fruitwood (apple, cherry) or hickory for a deeper profile. Smoke ribs uncovered for 5 hours until they develop a rich bark and take on color. If weather prevents smoking, skip to braising.
3. Preheat oven to 275–300°F. Place smoked (or raw) ribs in a Dutch oven or heavy roasting pan. Add red wine, water, boiled cider, bay leaf, garlic, and optional herbs. Liquid should come ¼–½ up the sides of the ribs. Cover tightly with lid or foil. Braise in oven for 2.5–3 hours until fork-tender.
4.Remove ribs from braising liquid. 
 Optional: Reduce braising liquid to a glaze or discard. 
 Brush ribs with Smooth Inferno sauce. 
 Finish under broiler or on grill for 5–10 minutes to caramelize and char the exterior.
5. Let rest 5–10 minutes. Slice between bones. 
 Serve with extra Smooth Inferno sauce on the side, a glass of red wine, and a nod to the storm that made it all possible.

recipes.RecipeName: Brie Bites with Back Olive Tapenade
recipes.Ingredients:
For Brie Bites:
1  sheet puff pastry, thawed but cold
6 oz. brie, cut into 12 cubes (about ¾ inch)
About ½ cup prepared Bacon Tapenade
1  egg, beaten (for egg wash)
1  sheet puff pastry, thawed but cold
6 oz. brie, cut into 12 cubes (about ¾ inch)
About ½ cup prepared Bacon Tapenade
1  egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Bacon Olive Tapenade
⅔ cup pitted Kalamata olives (or regular black olives)
2 tbsp. capers, rinsed and drained
1  anchovy fillet or ½ tsp. anchovy paste (optional)
1  small garlic clove, minced
1 tsp. fresh lemon juice
½ tsp. fresh thyme leaves (or a pinch dried)
1½ tbsp. olive oil
1  heaping tbsp. caramelized shallot, finely chopped (optional)
2 tbsp. crispy cooked bacon, finely chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. Prepare the tapenade: In a small food processor or mortar, combine olives, capers, anchovy, garlic, lemon juice, thyme, and shallot.
2. Pulse until coarsely chopped; do not purée.Add olive oil and pulse again briefly to bind. Fold in crumbles by hand. Season to taste with black pepper.
3. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
4. Assemble the bits: Cut puff pastry into 12 equal squares (approximately 2.5 inches each).
5. Place one brie cube and about 1/2 tsp. tapenade into the center of each square.
Fold corners up and pinch to seal the parcel.
Brush each with egg wash and add optional garnish.
Bake 15–18 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Let cool slightly before serving.
Optional Finish: Drizzle with balsamic glaze or serve with herbed honey.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cut puff pastry into 12 equal squares (approximately 2.5 inches each).
Place one brie cube and about 1/2 tsp. tapenade into the center of each square.
Fold corners up and pinch to seal the parcel.
Brush each with egg wash and add optional garnish.
Bake 15–18 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Let cool slightly before serving.
Optional Finish: Drizzle with balsamic glaze or serve with herbed honey.

recipes.Blurb: Buttermilk-brined pork medallions with a white wine–shallot–crème fraîche sauce and melting Gruyère
recipes.Ingredients:
For the Faux Veal Medallions:
1¼  1/2 lbs.pork tenderloin
1½ cups buttermilk
1 tbsp. kosher salt
1 tsp. cracked black pepper
2  bay leaves
3  garlic cloves, crushed
3  sprigs fresh thyme
All-purpose flour, for dredging
2 tbsp. unsalted butter
1 tbsp. olive oil
For the Savoyarde Sauce:
3 tbsp. shallots, finely minced
1  garlic clove, minced
¾ cup dry white wine (chardonnay works well)
¼ cup chicken stock
⅓ cup crème fraîche
2 tsp. Dijon or whole-grain mustard
⅓ cup Gruyère, grated (plus more for garnish, if desired)
1 tsp. fresh thyme leaves
Salt and pepper, to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. Slice pork into ½-inch medallions and gently lb. to ~¼ inch. Combine 1 cup buttermilk with 2 tsp. salt, in a bowl or resealable bag. Other spices (bay leaf, garlic, thyme) may be added. Submerge pork and refrigerate for 48 hours.
2. Remove pork from brine and pat dry. Lightly dredge each piece in flour, shaking off excess. Heat butter and oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork in batches, 2–3 minutes per side, until golden. Set aside and keep warm.
3. Lower heat to medium. In the same pan, sauté shallots until translucent; add garlic and cook briefly. Deglaze with white wine; simmer 3–4 minutes until reduced by half.
Add chicken stock and reduce slightly. Stir in crème fraîche and mustard; simmer until just thickened.
Add Gruyère and stir until melted. Season with thyme, salt, and pepper to taste.
4. Return pork to sauce. Spoon sauce over medallions and warm through gently.
Optional: add a final sprinkle of Gruyère and cover briefly to melt.

recipes.Ingredients:
½ cup high-quality extra virgin olive oil
½ tsp. dried rosemary
½ tsp. dried oregano
¼ tsp. fennel seeds, lightly crushed
½ tsp. dried garlic granules or toasted garlic powder
½ tsp. dill weed
Pinch of kosher salt
Optional: lemon zest, dried thyme, or a few black peppercorns for nuance
recipes.Procedure:
1. Gently warm the olive oil in a small pan (just until fragrant—not hot).
2. If using lemon zest, add it by itself and let steep for 10 minutes, then strain to remove. You just want a kiss of it!
3. Add garlic and herbs. Let infuse off heat for 5–10 minutes. If not needed immediately, let mixture steep at room temperature in a lightly-covered container for up to 12 days, for maximum richness.
4. Stir in salt, and pepper. Serve warm or at room temperature in a shallow dish.

recipes.RecipeName: Glazed Baby Carrots with Ginger, Brown Sugar & Hon
recipes.Blurb: A quietly comforting side dish—bright, buttery, and warm with spice.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 lb. baby carrots (trimmed if needed)
2 tbsp. unsalted butter
¼ cup water
¼ tsp. ground ginger (adjust to taste)
1 tbsp. brown sugar
1½ tbsp. honey
Pinch of salt (optional, to balance sweetness)
recipes.Procedure: In a wide skillet over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the carrots and sauté gently for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly glossy and just beginning to soften. Pour in the water, sprinkle in ground ginger, brown sugar, and honey. Stir to coat evenly. Cover loosely and simmer on low heat for 15–20 minutes, or until carrots are tender and the glaze has thickened to a silky sheen. Uncover, increase heat slightly, and stir until liquid reduces further into a sticky glaze that clings to the carrots. Taste and adjust seasoning. Transfer to a warm dish, optionally garnish with parsley or citrus zest. Optional Enhancements: Add a splash of orange juice instead of water for extra brightness. Toasted crushed pecans or almonds for crunch. A whisper of cinnamon if served alongside roast pork or poultry.
recipes.Notes:
*Optional Enhancements*  
- Add a splash of orange juice instead of water for extra brightness.  
- Toasted crushed pecans or almonds for crunch.  
- A whisper of cinnamon if served alongside roast pork or poultry.

recipes.Blurb: Torch-kissed peach halves glazed with rum citrus reduction and crowned with mascarpone vanilla cream.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
4  canned or previously frozen peach halves
¼ cup peach canning syrup or white grape juice (if using fresh peaches)
1  jigger (1.5 oz) dark rum
2 tbsp. brown sugar, divided
1 tsp. lemon juice
2  drops orange extract
4  whole cardamom seeds (to be removed before serving)
½ cup heavy whipping cream
¼ cup mascarpone cheese
1 tsp. vanilla sugar
4  dried or fresh cranberries (optional garnish)
recipes.Procedure:
Prepare Reduction: In a saucepan, combine juice or syrup, 1 tbsp. brown sugar, rum, lemon juice, orange extract, and cardamom. Simmer on low until thick and glossy. Cool and strain out seeds.
 Mascarpone Cream: Whip cream to soft peaks. Add mascarpone and vanilla sugar; beat to stiff peaks. Keep chilled.
 Caramelize Peaches: Place peaches flat side up. Sprinkle with 1 tbsp. brown sugar and torch until crisped and golden. Avoid overheating.
 Assemble: Spoon reduction around and over peaches. Fill cavities with cream. Top each with a cranberry for contrast.
recipes.Notes: Keep peaches chilled—torch only the tops to preserve texture. Serve on porcelain or slate for visual contrast. Best paired with Sauternes or late-harvest Riesling. Reduction may be prepared ahead and stored chilled; cream should be whipped fresh. Crisp sugar crust adds delicate bitterness to balance sweetness.

recipes.RecipeName: Naked Cake Base – Baker's Ratio Style
recipes.Blurb: Custom formulation for scalable holiday creations using baker's ratios for precise scaling and balance.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
All-purpose flour (100%)
Unsalted butter (85%)
Granulated sugar (100%)
Whole eggs (75%)
Whole milk (50%)
Baking powder (3%)
Kosher salt (1%)
Vanilla extract (2–3%, optional)
recipes.Procedure: Preheat oven to 175°C and prepare cake pans. Cream butter and sugar until pale and fluffy (3–5 min). Add eggs one at a time, beating gently. Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl. Alternate additions of dry mix and milk into the butter mixture, starting and ending with flour. Add vanilla extract if using. Pour into pans and bake until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

recipes.Blurb: Versatile fondant ideal for sculpting festive holly leaves and berries—smooth, pliable, and naturally colored.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. unflavored gelatin
¼ cup cold water
½ cup light corn syrup (or glucose)
1 tbsp. glycerin
1 tsp. vanilla extract
2  lbs.sifted confectioners’ sugar
½ tsp. vegetable shortening (plus extra for kneading)
Natural food coloring (as desired)
recipes.Procedure: Bloom gelatin in cold water; let stand for 5 minutes until firm. Microwave for 10 seconds and stir until fully melted. Combine with corn syrup, glycerin, and vanilla; mix until clear. Pour into well in 1½ lbs sugar; mix by hand or dough hook until soft dough forms. Add remaining sugar gradually, kneading until smooth and pliable. Tint with natural food coloring and divide for multiple tones if desired. Coat finished fondant lightly in shortening, wrap airtight, and rest overnight for sculpting holly decorations.
recipes.Notes: To sculpt holly leaves, roll fondant to ⅛" thickness, cut shapes freehand or with a cutter, and texture veins using a skewer. Drape over curved forms to dry for natural lift. Optional: dust with cornstarch for frosted look or brush with glycerin mixture for sheen. Pair leaves with sugared cranberries for botanical realism. Finished leaves should dry fully before cake placement and be affixed with softened fondant or glaze. Deepen color with layered green tones or score edges for fine detail. Designed to complement festive creations like Rumgeist No.1.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
3 tbsp. coconut oil (measured solid)
recipes.Procedure: Combine chocolate chips and coconut oil in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring thoroughly between each, until the mixture is smooth and fully melted. Allow to cool slightly, then drizzle over cold desserts such as ice cream, mousse, or layered jam/mascarpone fillings. The shell will harden upon contact with cold surfaces, forming a crisp, glossy layer.
recipes.Notes: The recipe yields enough shell for 8–10 servings depending on drizzle thickness. For a thinner shell, increase coconut oil slightly. Store leftovers in a sealed container and reheat gently. Ideal for integrating into holiday creations like Rumgeist No.1.

recipes.Blurb: Traditional Bavarian pretzels with chewy texture, rich brown crust, and signature twisted shape. This formula is ratio-perfect for scaling, shaping, and precision baking.
recipes.Author: From Bavarian sources
recipes.Ingredients:
100 % (480g) all-purpose flour
37½ % (180g) lukewarm milk
25 % (120g) lukewarm water
1.7 % (8g) brown sugar or malt extract
1.7 % (8g) instant yeast
8.8 % (42g) unsalted butter, melted
2.1 % (10g) salt
Soda Bath:
950 g water (˜4 cups)
36 g baking soda (˜3 tbsp)
Topping:
salt for garnish
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine milk, water, sugar/malt, and yeast. Let sit until foamy (~5 minutes).
2. Add flour, melted butter, and salt. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 minutes).
3. Cover and let rise until doubled in size (~1 hour).
4. Divide into 8 pieces (~120g each). Roll each into 16" ropes with thicker centers and tapered ends.
5. Twist into classic pretzel shapes. Place on parchment. Rest uncovered 30 minutes to develop a skin.
6. Simmer baking soda bath. Dip each pretzel for 5–10 seconds. Drain and place back on tray.
7. Score thick center with razor. Sprinkle coarse salt.
8. Bake at 390°F (200°C) for 18–20 minutes until deep mahogany brown.
9. Cool on wire rack. Serve fresh with mustard, Obatzda, or solitude.

recipes.Blurb: Traditional Bavarian pretzels with a deep brown crust, chewy interior, and iconic twisted shape. Best served fresh with coarse salt and good company.
recipes.Author: Adapted from PlatedCravings.com
recipes.Ingredients:
4 cups (480g) all-purpose flour
¾ cup (180g) lukewarm milk
½ cup (120g) lukewarm water
½  tsp. (8g) brown sugar or malt extract
½  tsp. (8g) instant yeast
3  tbsp. (42g) unsalted butter, melted
2  tsp. (10g) salt
Soda Bath:
4 cups (950g) water
3  tbsp. (36g) baking soda
Topping:
salt for sprinkling
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine milk, water, sugar/malt, and yeast. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
2. Add flour, melted butter, and salt. Knead into a smooth, elastic dough (~8 minutes).
3. Cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
4. Divide dough into 8 equal pieces (~120g each). Roll into 16" ropes, bulging in the center and tapered at ends.
5. Twist into classic pretzel shape. Let rise uncovered 30 minutes. Optionally air-dry to form a skin.
6. Preheat oven to 390°F (200°C). Bring water to a simmer and add baking soda.
7. Dip each pretzel for 5–10 seconds. Drain and place on parchment-lined tray.
8. Slash the thick center with a razor. Sprinkle coarse salt.
9. Bake for 18–20 minutes until deep mahogany brown. Cool on a rack and serve warm.

recipes.RecipeName: Soft Burger and Hot Dog Buns
recipes.Blurb: One dough. Two shapes. Perfect softness.
recipes.Author: Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
TANGZHONG
2 tbsp. + 1 tsp. all-purpose flour
3 tbsp. milk

DOUGH
312 g. all-purpose flour
192 ml warm milk
1 large egg
2 tbsp. + 1 tsp. soft butter
1 tbsp. + 2 tsp. sugar
1½ tsp. salt
2 tsp. instant yeast
All of the tangzhong
recipes.Procedure:
1. Make the tangzhong: whisk flour and milk over gentle heat until thickened into a smooth paste. Cool to lukewarm. 
2. Mix the dough: combine warm milk, egg, butter, sugar, salt, yeast, and the cooled tangzhong. Add flour. Mix until a soft, slightly tacky dough forms. Knead only until smooth; avoid building strong gluten. 
3. First rise: cover and let rise until very puffy. 
4. Divide and place into your rings/forms. 
5. Second rise: let rise until extremely puffy. 
6. Bake at 350°F for 15–18 minutes, until pale gold. Do not overbrown.
recipes.Notes:
For hot dog buns: 53g/bun, makes 12 buns
For hamburger buns, 60g/bun, makes 11 buns
For sandwich rolls, divide dough into 8 equal portions

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 lb. ground beef
2 tbsp. tomato paste
1 tsp. ground cumin
1 tbsp. ancho chili powder
½ tsp. smoked paprika
½ tsp. garlic powder
½ tsp. onion powder
¼ tsp. ground cinnamon (optional)
pinch oregano
1 tsp. yellow mustard
1 tsp. Worcestershire sauce
½ tsp. salt, or to taste
pinch brown sugar (optional)
¾ cup beef broth or water
¾ cup passata, or to taste
recipes.Procedure: Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it into very fine crumbles. Drain excess fat if desired. Stir in tomato paste, followed by all dry seasonings, and cook for 1–2 minutes to bloom the spices. Add mustard, Worcestershire, and broth. Stir to combine, then simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes until thickened but still spoonable. Adjust seasoning to taste and serve warm atop hot dogs.
recipes.Notes: Freeze leftovers in 1/4-cup portions for quick future use. This chili is beanless by design and tailored for topping rather than bowl service. Optional garnishes include diced onions, shredded cheddar, jalapeño slices, or green chile relish. Built to complement Aaron-standard hot dog buns and designed for structural integrity under duress.

recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup sugar
3 tbsp. cornstarch
2  14.5-oz cans red tart pie cherries
2 cups fresh or frozen cranberries
¼ tsp. nutmeg
¼ tsp. red food coloring (optional)
¼ tsp. almond extract (optional)
1 tbsp. lemon juice
1 tbsp. unsalted butter
2 crusts for 9-in pie
recipes.Procedure:
1.Preheat oven to 400º.
2. Drain the cherries and reserve the juice from one can only.  In a saucepan, stir the cherry juice into the craberries. Cook over low heat, until cranberries and cherry juice have reduced into a thick syrup.  Stir in half the sugar.  If necessary, adjust thickness with water or cornstarch.  Remove from heat.
3.  Gently stir in the remaining sugar, cherries and optional ingredients.  Pour filling into pastry-lined pie pan.  Dot with butter.  Adjust crust, seal and vent.  Bake 45 min. or until crust browns and filling begins to bubble.  If necessary, cover edges with aluminum foil during last 15 min to prevent over-browning.  Cool pie several hours to allow filling to thicken before slicing.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup passata or tomato pureé
¼ cup white wine vinegar
1 tbsp. Dijon mustard
2 tbsp. molasses
¼ cup raisins, soaked for 15 min.
2 tbsp. orange juice
½ tsp. orange peel
½ tsp. salt
½ tsp. celery seed
⅛ tsp. ground nutmeg
⅛ tsp. ground allspice
recipes.Procedure:
1. In a saucepan, combine passata, vinegar, mustard, molasses, pureéd raisins, and orange juice/zest.
2. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Stir frequently.
3. Cook uncovered for 20–30 minutes until slightly thickened and cohesive.
4. Optional: Blend again for smoothness, then strain for silky texture.
5. Taste and adjust salt or acid if needed. Bottle while warm. Refrigerate once cool.
recipes.Notes:
- Use within 3 weeks for peak flavor. Flavor intensifies after 24 hours in the fridge.
- Great as a marinade, glaze, or steak-side whisper.

🖤 Smooth. Tangy. Complex. Like the original—only smarter.

recipes.Ingredients:
6 oz. dry pasta (rotini, fusilli, or elbow macaroni)
2 oz. Gruyère
2 oz. white Cheddar
2 oz. Parmesan or Grana Padano
2 cups heavy cream
1 tsp. vegetable oil
Kosher salt, to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. Cook pasta in salted water until just al dente. Drain and toss with oil.
2. Grate cheeses and divide into two portions: 40% for sauce, 60% for topping.
3. In a deep pan, bring cream to a gentle simmer. Add pasta and stir.
4. Gradually stir in the smaller cheese portion until melted and smooth.
5. Transfer mixture to a baking dish. Top with remaining cheese.
6. Broil 3–5 minutes until bubbly and golden brown.
7. Let rest briefly before serving.
recipes.Notes:
Optional Enhancements:
Top with sourdough breadcrumbs for crunch.
Add a pinch of nutmeg or Dijon mustard to the cream.
Layer caramelized onions or apples beneath the pasta for a sweet-savory twist.Add additional notes

recipes.Blurb: Inspired by Mezzetta's bright, crunchy profile with sharper heat and balanced spice.
recipes.Author: Aaron's Archive
recipes.Ingredients:
5 cups distilled white vinegar (5% acidity)
2 cups water
2 heads cauliflower, broken into florets
Baby carrots, halved
Sweet peppers, sliced into strips
1 small red onion, cut into bite-sized pieces
Celery, sliced
Thai Dragon chilis, sliced
4 cloves garlic, sliced
4 tsp. mustard seed
4 tsp. peppercorns
4 tsp. coriander seeds
4 tsp. dill seeds
½ tsp. turmeric per jar
½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes per jar
¼ tsp. fennel seed per jar (optional)
1–2 tsp. sugar per jar
4 whole hot peppers
4 bay leaves
recipes.Procedure: Steam-blanch cauliflower florets for 2 minutes to preserve color and texture. Wash all vegetables. Place in large pan and cover with canning salt; let sit overnight. Rinse thoroughly and allow to air-dry briefly. Sterilize 4 quart jars and lids. Mix vinegar, water, and salt (to taste) and bring to a boil. Fill jars with vegetables and ¼ of the spices per jar, including turmeric, red pepper flakes, sugar, and optional fennel. Fill with boiling vinegar mixture and seal. For maximum crispness, refrigerate immediately after cooling—do not process in boiling water. Store in refrigerator for at least 2 weeks before eating. Keeps well for up to 2 years if sealed and undisturbed.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
For the puddings:
90 g. all-purpose flour
1¼ tsp. baking powder
¼ tsp. baking soda
¼ tsp. salt
1½ tsp. mixed spices (e.g., cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, clove)
Zest of 1 small orange or ½ large
65 g. unsalted butter, melted
⅓ cup molasses
3 tbsp. brown sugar
2 large eggs
1 tbsp. dark rum (or milk)
0–2 Tbsp milk or orange juice (adjust for batter consistency)
¾ cup fresh apple, peeled and diced medium, ½ in.
1¼ cup fresh cranberries, precooked til soft
Lemon-rum icing

For garnish:
2 tbsp. chopped pecans
recipes.Procedure:
1. Butter pudding molds; place parchment rounds at base
2. In a large bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and spices.
3. In a separate bowl, combine melted butter, molasses, brown sugar, eggs, and zest.
4. Stir wet into dry until just combined. Add milk or juice to loosen batter as needed.
5. Fold in chopped apples and cranberries.
6. Spoon into prepared molds, filling ¾ full.
7. Cover molds with parchment and foil, secure with string or bands if steaming traditionally.
8. Steam for 60–75 minutes, checking for firmness and spring-back.
9. Cool briefly (about 20 min), then unmold carefully.
10. Top with lemon-rum icing and sprinkle with chopped pecans.

recipes.Author: christinascucina.com
recipes.Ingredients:
½ cup (113 g) good quality butter (see notes)
1 heaped cup (200 g) dark brown sugar
½ cup (70 g) all purpose flour
½ tsp. baking powder
2  eggs
1 tsp. mixed spice (see recipe in notes if you don't have any)
2 cups (100 g) fresh breadcrumbs
1 cup (150 g) sultanas (golden raisins)
1 cup (150 g) raisins (note: I soaked my raisins in brandy, overnight)
½ cup (60 g) Zante currants
1 small apple, peeled, cored and grated
finely grated rind of one fresh orange (or lemon)
juice of one fresh orange or lemon, made up to 5 oz. (150 ml) with brandy or rum
(optional - 3 Tbsp mixed candied peel, chopped)
For the mixed spice:
½ tsp. cinnamon ground
½ tsp. nutmeg ground
½ tsp. coriander dried, ground spice
¼ tsp. ginger ground, dried spice (not fresh)
¼ tsp. allspice ground
⅛ tsp. mace ground
⅛ tsp. cloves ground
recipes.Procedure:
1. Butter the pudding bowl and line the bottom with a disc of parchment or waxed paper, and butter the paper, too.
2. Beat the suet/butter and sugar together until soft.
3. Add the flour, eggs, and spice until mixed. Then add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
4. Put the mixture into the buttered bowl and flatten the top.
Cut a disc of waxed or parchment paper the size of the top, butter it and place on top of the pudding mixture.
5. Tear a piece of parchment paper and aluminum foil, large enough to cover the top of the bowl, and go halfway down the sides, and place the foil on top of the parchment. Create a pleat down the center, so that the pudding will have space to expand when cooking.
6. Place the paper and foil over the pudding basin, then tie some string under the lip of the bowl, leaving extra string to tie over the top to form a handle, tying it on the opposite end. If you don't have a steamer, like me, place a trivet in a pot and fill the water so that it's halfway up the bowl and use a tight fitting lid.
7. Steam for 6 hours, checking the water level once an hour or so, and topping it up.
8. Once you've taken the bowl out of the pot, remove the aluminum foil and waxed/parchment paper, wipe the bowl and replace with clean paper. Store in a cool place.
To serve: you can steam it for another two hours, OR simply microwave it for a few minutes until it's piping hot! Let stand for a few minutes before removing from the bowl. Place on a heatproof serving dish and douse with brandy. Carefully light the pudding (please do this in a safe area), then when the flame extinguishes, cut and serve with brandy sauce or butter, whipped cream, or custard.

recipes.Ingredients:
Dough:
1 cup warm milk (110°F)
2¼ tsp. instant yeast (1 packet)
¼ cup granulated sugar
1  egg
¼ cup unsalted butter, melted
½ tsp. salt
3½ cups all-purpose flour
Filling:
½ cup brown sugar
2 tbsp. ground cinnamon
¼ cup unsalted butter, softened
Vanilla Glaze:
1 cup powdered sugar
2 tbsp. milk
½ tsp. vanilla extract
Pinch of salt (optional)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine warm milk and yeast. Let sit 5 minutes.
2. Add sugar, egg, melted butter, and salt. Mix well.
3. Gradually add flour until a soft dough forms. Knead 5–7 minutes.
4. Cover and let rise 45–60 minutes until doubled.
5. Roll dough into 14x9" rectangle. Spread butter, sprinkle cinnamon sugar.
6. Roll up tightly, slice into 12 rolls.
7. Place in greased 9x13" pan. Rest 15 minutes while oven preheats to 375°F.
8. Bake 20–25 minutes until golden.
9. Whisk glaze ingredients and drizzle over warm rolls.

recipes.Ingredients:
Filling:
1 cup diced carrots
1 cup small broccoli florets
½ cup sliced celery
½ cup sliced green beans (blanched if fresh)
1 tbsp. olive oil
Salt, pepper, and a pinch of thyme or marjoram
Sauce:
2 tbsp. butter
2 tbsp. flour
1 cup light vegetable stock (or chicken, if preferred)
¼ cup dry white wine
1 tsp. Dijon mustard
Salt, white pepper, and a whisper of nutmeg or lemon zest
2 sheets puff pastry, thawed
1 egg yolk + 1 tbsp. milk (egg wash)
Optional: a sprinkle of grated Gruyère or aged cheddar
recipes.Procedure:
1. Roast carrots and broccoli at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes until tender and caramelized. Sauté celery and green beans briefly in a pan with olive oil until just softened. Combine all and let cool.
2. Make a blond roux with butter and flour.
3. Gradually whisk in warm stock and wine.
4. Simmer until thickened (~10 min).
5. Stir in mustard and seasonings. Let cool before mixing with vegetables.
6. Cut each pastry into 4 rectangles.
7. Spoon cooled filling onto one of four rectangles; top with cheese if using.
8. Cover rectangle with second rectangle of puff pastry, seal edges, and brush with egg wash.
9. Chill 15 minutes before baking, or freeze on a sheet lined with parchment.
10. Bake from frozen at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes until golden and puffed.
recipes.Notes:
Shell Format Adaptation:
• Bake shells according to package instructions until puffed and golden.
• Scoop out the center “lid” gently to create a cavity.
• Fill with warm vegetable-velouté mixture, optionally topped with cheese.
• Return to oven briefly (5–7 minutes at 375°F) to melt cheese and marry flavors.
• Serve with the pastry lid perched jauntily or tucked alongside like a croissant epilogue.

recipes.Author: bakingamoment.com
recipes.Ingredients:
2¼ cups all-purpose flour
1 tsp. salt
1¼ cups unsalted butter (2 1/2 sticks), cold
5-6 oz. cold water
recipes.Procedure:
Place the flour and salt in a large bowl and whisk to combine.
Cut the cold butter into 1/4-inch slices and add to the flour mixture, tossing to coat.
Stir in the cold water until a thick dough forms.
Gather the dough into a ball, flatten it into a disk-shape, and wrap in plastic wrap.
Chill for 1 hour in the fridge, or 20 to 30 minutes in the freezer.
Unwrap the dough, dust the work surface with flour, and roll the dough into a rough rectangle shape.
Fold the dough in thirds, like a letter.
Turn 90 degrees, roll and fold again.

Repeat about 2 to 4 times, wrap the dough in plastic wrap, and chill for 2 hours or overnight.

recipes.RecipeName: Ham and Cheese Puff Pastry Filling
recipes.Blurb: A creamy, fork-friendly filling of diced ham bound in cheese sauce, perfect for puff pastry.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
2 cups diced ham (½-inch cubes)
1 cup mixed peas and carrots, or other
1 tbsp. butter
1 tbsp. flour
½ cup warm milk
½ cup grated sharp cheddar or Gruyère
1 tbsp. Dijon mustard
Salt & pepper to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. Melt butter in a small saucepan, stir in flour, and cook 1 minute.
2. Whisk in warm milk gradually until smooth and thickened. Add mustard and mix well.
3. Stir in grated cheese until melted and creamy. Season with salt, pepper to taste.
4. Fold in diced ham. Mixture should be thick—spreadable, not runny.
5. Let cool slightly until firm enough to spoon into pastry without leaking.
6. Place filling in pastry squares, seal, and bake until golden.
recipes.Notes:
Chill the filling briefly before assembly for easier handling. 
For extra flavor, add a spoon of Dijon mustard to the sauce. 
Crown baked pastries with basil or roasted cherry tomato for festive presentation.

recipes.Blurb: Bright, aromatic, and clean; pairs well with cream or cheese sauces.
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
Zest of 1 lemon or orange
1 tsp. rosemary (dried or fresh, finely chopped)
1 tsp. thyme
½ tsp. garlic powder
1 tsp. kosher salt
½ tsp. black pepper
recipes.Procedure: Combine all ingredients. Rub evenly over dried turkey breast after brining. Rest uncovered in fridge before roasting.
recipes.Notes: Provides a bright Mediterranean profile; works well with poultry and translates into cream-based sauces.

recipes.Blurb: Warm, tangy, golden hue; complements Gruyère or cheddar sauces.
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. Dijon mustard (binder)
1 tsp. ground coriander
½ tsp. turmeric
1 tsp. kosher salt
½ tsp. white pepper
recipes.Procedure: Mix dry spices. Coat turkey breast lightly with Dijon mustard, then apply rub. Rest uncovered in fridge before roasting.
recipes.Notes: Creates a warm, golden flavor profile; mustard acts as binder and adds tang.

recipes.Blurb: Earthy, savory, subtle smokiness; adds depth without overpowering cheese sauces.
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tsp. smoked paprika
1 tsp. garlic powder
½ tsp. cumin
1 tsp. kosher salt
½ tsp. black pepper
recipes.Procedure: Combine all ingredients. Rub evenly over dried turkey breast after brining. Rest uncovered in fridge before roasting.
recipes.Notes: Provides earthy depth and subtle smokiness; versatile for poultry and adaptable to sauces.

recipes.Blurb: Smoky, citrusy, and herbal; chipotle anchors the blend while coriander and oregano add nuance.
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tsp. ground chipotle chili powder
1 tsp. ground coriander
1 tsp. dried oregano
½ tsp. garlic powder
1 tsp. kosher salt
½ tsp. black pepper
recipes.Procedure: Combine all ingredients thoroughly. Rub evenly over dried poultry after brining. Rest uncovered in fridge before roasting or grilling.
recipes.Notes: Chipotle provides smoky depth, coriander adds citrusy warmth, and oregano contributes herbal brightness. Works well on chicken thighs or turkey breast.

recipes.Blurb: Classic laminated dough with butter block.
recipes.Ingredients:
Dough:
4¼ cups (510g) all-purpose flour
1½ tsp. table salt
4 tbsp. (57g) cold unsalted butter, cubed
1¼ cups (284g) cold water
Butter block:
28 tbsp. (396g) unsalted butter, room temp
½ cup (60g) all-purpose flour
recipes.Procedure:
1. Dough: In mixer bowl, combine flour + salt. Add cold butter; mix with flat beater until coarse. Add cold water; mix until shaggy dough forms. Knead briefly until tacky. Shape into 9" square, wrap, chill 30–60 min.
2. Butter block: Beat butter + flour until smooth. Spread into 8" square on parchment, cover, chill 30 min.
3. Laminate: Roll dough to 12" square. Place butter block at 45° angle, fold corners over, seal. Roll packet to 20"x10". Fold in thirds (like letter), rotate 90°. This is 1 turn.
4. Repeat rolling/folding for 6 turns total, chilling 15 min every 2 turns if needed.
5. Wrap and chill 1–4 hrs (up to 2 days). Freeze up to 6 months; thaw overnight in fridge before use.
recipes.Notes:
• Keep dough and butter cool but pliable.  
• Visible butter layers = flakiness.  
• Roll, cut, and shape as recipe directs.

recipes.RecipeName: Broccoli and Cauliflower Puff Pastry Filling
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1½ cups broccoli florets
1½ cups cauliflower florets.
1 tbsp. butter
1 tbsp. flour
½ cup warm milk
½ cup grated sharp cheddar or Gruyère
1 tbsp. Dijon mustard
Salt & pepper to taste
recipes.Procedure:
1. Blanch the broccoli florets for 2 minutes in boiling water; plunge immediately into ice water to stop cooking. Allow to drain and dry on towel.
2. Blanch the cauliflower florets for 3 minutes in boiling water; plunge into ice water. Drain and dry.
3. Melt butter in a small saucepan, stir in flour, and cook 1 minute.
4. Whisk in warm milk gradually until smooth and thickened. Add mustard and mix well.
5. Stir in grated cheese until melted and creamy. Season with salt, pepper to taste.
6. Fold in vegetables.. Mixture should be thick—spreadable, not runny.
7. Chill mixture briefly until firm enough to spoon into pastry without leaking.
8. Place filling in pastry squares, seal, and bake until golden, or wrap and freeze for later.

recipes.Blurb: Simple reduction-glazed carrots with optional aromatic, citrus, herb, and sweetener variations.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 lb. baby carrots
Water to cover
1 tbsp. brown sugar (or alternate sweetener)
recipes.Procedure:
Place carrots in a saucepan and add enough water to cover. Add brown sugar (or chosen sweetener). Add any selected spice, citrus, or herb options if using. Bring to a simmer and cook until the liquid reduces to a glossy glaze and the carrots are tender. Adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt or a small amount of acid if desired. Serve warm.

Options:
SPICE OPTIONS (choose 0–1)
Cardamom — pinch ground OR 2–3 cracked pods
Coriander seed — 3–5 lightly crushed seeds
Allspice — 1 whole berry
Star anise — 1/4 to 1/2 pod
Ginger — 1/8 tsp ground

CITRUS OPTIONS (choose 0–1)
Orange zest — 1–2 strips
Lemon zest — 1 strip
Orange juice — replace part of water with 2–4 tbsp
Lemon juice — 1–2 tsp added near end

HERB OPTIONS (choose 0–1)
Thyme — 1 fresh sprig
Bay leaf — 1 leaf
Tarragon — tiny pinch or 1 small sprig

SWEETENER OPTIONS (choose 1)
Brown sugar — 1 tbsp
Honey — 1 tbsp
Maple syrup — 1 tbsp

BALANCE ADJUSTERS (optional)
Salt — pinch
Vinegar (rice, cider, white wine) — 1/2 tsp near end
Lemon juice — 1–2 tsp near end

TECHNIQUE VARIATION (optional)
Brown carrots first in a little butter or oil before adding liquid
recipes.Notes: Reduce until the glaze clings to the carrots and the pan shows clear syrupy trails when stirred.

recipes.Blurb: This recipe is ALL about technique.  Take your time to do it right.
recipes.Author: sainsburysmagazine.co.uk
recipes.Ingredients:
1½ kg. potatoes (Russet or Yukon Gold), peeled
110 g. unsalted butter
Kosher salt
recipes.Procedure:
GET AHEAD: The day before serving, prepare to the end of step 4 then bake for 30 mins rather than 20 mins. Cool and store at room temperature. Reheat, covered, for 20 mins, then uncovered for 5-10 mins to crisp the top.

If you have a single oven, prepare and part-cook the pommes Anna the day before (see Get Ahead) so that you don’t have to juggle oven temperatures and cooking times.

1. Slice the potatoes thinly, using a mandoline or processor if you have one, or cut into 2 mm (this is important!) slices by hand with a large sharp knife. Rinse the sliced potatoes in cold water to remove the starch, then pat dry on a clean towel or with kitchen paper. Melt the butter in a small pan, then pour into a bowl, discarding the last milky-looking bit that’s in the bottom of the pan.
2. Add 3 tbsp. of the melted butter to a large heavy ovenproof skillet (about 21cm base diameter, or see our tip below. Swirl around to coat, then neatly arrange a layer of potato slices in the bottom of the pan – this will be the presentation side when it’s cooked, so take some time over it. Brush some more butter over the potatoes and sprinkle lightly with kosher salt (sprinkle slighly more heavily on the first layer). Add another layer of slices. Repeat until the pan is full, reserving enough butter to brush onto a large square of foil.
3. Cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until the base is golden, shaking the pan every few minutes so that the potatoes don’t stick. Preheat the oven to 390° F.
4. Cover the pan with the prepared foil, buttered-side down. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
5. Remove the foil and cook for another 20 minutes or until golden-brown on top and the potatoes are cooked through when pierced with a sharp knife or skewer. Leave to settle for 10 minutes before turning out onto a platter to serve, cut into wedges.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
6–8 dried habaneros, stemmed (soaked in warm water 20 min to soften)
4–6 dried mixed hot peppers (e.g., cayenne, Thai, pequin—adjust for heat and complexity)
1 cup passata (smooth, strained tomato puree)
2 cloves garlic, roasted or sautéed
1 tbsp. apple cider vinegar (or white vinegar for sharper tang)
1 tsp. sugar (optional, to round acidity)
½ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. smoked paprika (optional, for depth)
1 tbsp. olive oil (for blending and mouthfeel)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Rehydrate peppers: Soak dried habaneros and mixed peppers in warm water until pliable. Drain, reserving a bit of soak water.
2. Sauté garlic in olive oil until golden. Optional: add a pinch of cumin or coriander seed for complexity.
3. Blend: Combine rehydrated peppers, passata, garlic, vinegar, salt, sugar, and paprika. Add a splash of soak water if needed.
4. Simmer: Pour into a non-reactive saucepan and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes to meld flavors and thicken slightly.
5. Final blend: Blitz again for silky texture. Adjust salt, vinegar, or sugar to taste.
6. Bottle and refrigerate: Keeps for weeks. For longer shelf life, increase vinegar to 2 tbsp. and simmer longer.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
3 lb. chicken wings, disjointed
3 tbsp. baking powder (NOT soda)
2¼ tsp. kosher salt
recipes.Procedure:
1. Pat wings dry—paper towels, no mercy. Toss raw wings in a mix of baking powder + salt (about 1 tbsp. baking powder plus 3/4 to 1 tsp. salt per lb. of wings).
2. You can add a pinch of black pepper or smoked paprika if you want a hint of pre-sauce flavor. This raises the skin’s pH and draws moisture to the surface, helping it crisp in the oven.
3. Lay them on a wire rack over a sheet pan—skin side up, spaced out like they’re sunbathing.
4. Refrigerate uncovered for a few hours or overnight if time allows. That dry chill is your secret weapon.
5. Start at 250°F for 30 minutes to render fat. Then crank it to 425°F (convection if possible) for 40–50 minutes until golden and crisp. Flip halfway through for even crisping.

recipes.Blurb: If cooking for two, we suggest you make two small loaves.  Enjoy one now and freeze one for another meal.
recipes.Author: Rosemary Robbins
recipes.Ingredients:
1½ lbs.ground beef
1 cup dry bread crumbs
1 tsp. salt
¼ tsp. pepper
2  eggs
1 tsp. minced onion.
1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce, divided (or use Passata)
2 tbsp. brown sugar
2 tbsp. vinegar (see notes)
½ cup granulated sugar
2 tsp. prepared mustard (see notes)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Mix together beef, bread crumbs, salt, pepper and eggs. Add onion and half the tomato sauce and knead to mix well.
2. Form into a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan (or two smaller loaf pans).
3. Bake at 350º for 50 minutes.
4. Meanwhile, combine remaining tomato sauce, brown sugar, vinegar, sugar and mustard. Bring to a boil. Pour over meat loaf and bake 10 minutes more.
recipes.Notes:
1) Try different vinegars to add nuance to the meatloaf: apple cider, red wine or other.
2) Try Dijon or brown mustard for a change.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
¾ cup passata
¼ cup red wine
¼ tsp. Worcestershire sauce
⅛ tsp. garlic powder
1 tbsp. brown sugar
½ tsp. sea salt
⅛ tsp. ground black pepper
recipes.Procedure: Mix ingredients together in small sauce pan and simmer until it reaches the desired thickness
recipes.Notes: If you prefer your ketchup very thick, reduce the amount of salt, as salt becomes more pronounced as the ketchup becomes thicker.

recipes.Blurb: A dark, paprika-forward braise designed for a 35-oz pork shoulder, yielding tender, cohesive pieces without shredding.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
35 oz. pork shoulder, cut into large chunks after brining
2 large onions, sliced
2 tbsp. tomato paste
2 tbsp. sweet paprika
½ tsp. hot paprika (optional)
½ cup red wine
½ to 3/4 cup white wine
1 to 1 1/4 cups broth (beef or chicken)
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 bay leaf
1 tsp. dried thyme or marjoram
Salt (preferably smoked) and black pepper, to taste
2 tbsp. oil or fat for browning
recipes.Procedure:
1.Pat the buttermilk-brined pork dry and cut into large, palm-sized pieces. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork well on all sides, then remove and set aside. 
2. Add the sliced onions to the pot and cook until softened and beginning to color. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1-2 minutes until darkened. Add garlic and paprika, stirring briefly to bloom the spices. Pour in the red and white wine, scraping up any browned bits. 
3. Add enough broth to bring the total liquid to about 2 to 2 1/2 cups. Return the pork to the pot, add bay leaf and thyme, and bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and braise in a 300°F oven for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, or until the pork is tender but still holds together cleanly when cut. Rest the meat in the sauce for 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.Notes: Browning the tomato paste is essential for achieving a deep, brick-red sauce. Adjust the ratio of red to white wine based on availability; paprika and tomato paste will maintain the dark color. A small splash of vinegar at the end can brighten the flavors. Serve with noodles, potatoes, or crusty bread.

recipes.Author: Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
4 tbsp. peanut butter
2 tbsp. soy sauce
2 tbsp. lime juice
2 tsp. brown sugar or honey
1 large grated garlic clove
pinch of chili flakes
recipes.Procedure:
1. Whisk all ingredients together in a small bowl.
2. Add warm water a tsp. at a time until it becomes a pourable, silky sauce.
3. Toss with steamed broccoli, noodles, or whatever you choose.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
1 cup chilled whipped cream
1 lb. mascarpone
⅓ cup sugar
24  ladyfingers
4 oz. creme de cacao
1 tsp. vanilla
2 squares whilte chocolate, grated finely
1 square 78% cacao chocolate
recipes.Procedure:
1. A half-hour before you begin, chill blender container or bowl and beaters.
2. Pour cream into bowl or blender and whip until it holds its shape (4-5 min.)
3. In a large bowl, mix mascarpone, sugare, vanilla and white chocolate. Fold in whipped cream.
4. Briefly dip ladyfingers in creme de cacao and arrange in a 9" square baking dish. Do not saturate: a brief dip is all that's required. Spoon half of the mascarpone/cream mixture on top.
5. Repeat step 4, adding second layer of ladyfingers/mascarpone.
6. Using a microplane grater, grate the 78% cacao chocolate over the top. Cover dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate 4 hours to overnight. Can be kept, refrigerated, up to 24 hours.

recipes.Blurb: Traditional Bavarian pretzels dipped in a 3% lye solution for the classic deep brown crust and unmistakable flavor.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
500 g. all-purpose flour
10 g. salt
20 g. butter, softened
7 g. dry yeast (or 20 g. fresh yeast)
250-280 ml ice-cold water
1-2 tsp. barley malt syrup (optional but traditional)
Pretzel salt for topping
30 g. food-grade lye per 1 liter cold water (3% solution)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine the cold water, yeast, and barley malt syrup (if using) and stir to dissolve.
2. In a separate bowl, mix the flour and salt, then add the butter and rub until coarse crumbs form. 
3. Add the yeast mixture and knead 6-8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Let rise 1 hour at room temperature or refrigerate overnight for improved flavor
4.. Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a rope 24-30 inches long with thin ends and a thicker center. Shape into pretzels by forming a U, crossing the ends twice, and pressing them onto the belly. Chill the shaped pretzels in the refrigerator or freezer until firm
5. Prepare a 3% lye bath by carefully adding the lye to cold water. Dip each pretzel for 10-15 seconds, remove, drain, and sprinkle with pretzel salt. Slash the belly lengthwise with a single clean cut. 
6..Bake at 450-500° for 10-5 minutes until deep mahogany brown.
recipes.Notes: Use stainless steel, glass, or high-grade plastic for the lye bath. Wear gloves and protective eyewear. Always add lye to water, never water to lye. The belly slash should be a 2-3 inch horizontal cut along the thickest part of the lower curve. Chilling the shaped pretzels helps them keep their form during dipping. Authentic pretzel salt is recommended for proper crunch and appearance.

recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
4 tbsp. soy sauce
4 tbsp. stock
1 tbsp. sherry
¾ tsp. sugar
a few drops of sesame oil
a pinch of white pepper
recipes.Procedure: Mix ingredients in a small pan over low heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes aromatic. Serve warm.

recipes.Blurb: A clean, intentional cioppino built around cod, shrimp, mussels, canned clams, and shrimp-shell stock.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp. olive oil
1 medium onion, finely diced
1 fennel bulb, diced (optional)
4-6 garlic cloves, minced
1 tsp. red pepper flakes
2 tbsp. tomato paste
1 cup dry white wine
1 can (14-15 oz) crushed tomatoes
3-4 cups seafood stock (fish, shrimp shell, etc.)
1 bay leaf
1 strip lemon zest
1 lb. cod, cut into large chunks
1 lb. mussels in shell (pasteurized, uncooked)
8 oz. shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 can chopped clams, drained
Salt and pepper to taste
Chopped parsley for finishing
recipes.Procedure:
1. Heat olive oil in a heavy pot. Add onion and fennel and cook until softened.
2. Add garlic and red pepper flakes and cook briefly. Stir in tomato paste and cook until darkened. Deglaze with white wine.
3. Add crushed tomatoes, stock, bay leaf, and lemon zest. Simmer 20-30 minutes. Season to taste with salt.
4. Add cod and simmer 5-7 minutes. 
5. Add mussels, cover, and cook until they open.
6. Add shrimp and canned clams and cook 2-3 minutes more. Adjust seasoning. Finish with parsley and a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.Notes: Mussels are served in-shell; diners remove them with a fork or by using an empty shell as tongs. Empty shells remain in the bowl. This version emphasizes a clean broth, proper sequencing of seafood, and avoids overcooking.

recipes.Blurb: Scaled for a smaller package of short ribs without losing depth or richness.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
3 short ribs (about 1.5–2 lb. total)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
½  carrot, chopped
½ stalk celery, chopped
½ medium onion, chopped
½  tomato, cut into fourths
2 cloves garlic, chopped
2 tsp. tomato paste
2 tbsp. extra virgin olive oil
⅔ cup dry white wine
⅔ cup unsalted broth (beef or chicken)
1 small sprig thyme or rosemary (optional)
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat oven to 325º. Pat ribs dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
  Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high until just smoking. Brown ribs well on all sides; transfer to a covered baking dish.
2. Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1–2 tbsp. Add carrot, celery, onion and garlic; cook until lightly browned.
  Add tomato paste and cook 1–2 minutes until slightly darkened. Deglaze with a splash of broth, scraping up browned bits.
  Add wine, remaining broth, tomato pieces and herb sprig (if using). Bring to a full boil.
3. Pour mixture over ribs, cover tightly and bake at 325º for about 3 hours, until meat is very tender.
4. Remove ribs to a plate. Strain braising liquid into a saucepan; discard solids. Skim off as much fat as possible.
  Reduce liquid over medium heat by about half, until glossy and slightly thickened.
5.Remove meat from bones and trim tendon and gristle. (Meat and sauce can be packaged together and kept up to a week.)
  Arrange meat on a plate and spoon the reduced sauce over the top.

recipes.RecipeName: Tuscan White Beans with Garlic & Rosemary
recipes.Blurb: Silky cannellini beans gently warmed with garlic, rosemary, and olive oil; a perfect Mediterranean counterpoint to citrus chicken.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
2 cans cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
3 tbsp. olive oil
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 tsp. fresh rosemary, finely chopped
¼ tsp. crushed red pepper (optional)
¼ cup chicken broth or water
Salt and pepper to taste
1 tsp. lemon juice
recipes.Procedure: Warm olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add garlic and rosemary; cook gently until fragrant but not browned. Add beans, broth, and crushed red pepper if using. Simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are creamy and warmed through. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.Notes: Do not let the garlic brown; the flavor should stay soft and aromatic. A drizzle of extra olive oil at the end is traditional.

recipes.Blurb: Crisp-edged, tender potatoes roasted with olive oil, garlic, rosemary, and oregano; ideal for soaking up Mediterranean sauces.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott with Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
2 lbs.yukon Gold potatoes, cut into wedges
3 tbsp. olive oil
3 cloves garlic, smashed
1 tsp. dried oregano
1 tsp. dried rosemary or 2 tsp. fresh
½ tsp. salt
¼ tsp. black pepper
Optional: thin slices of lemon
recipes.Procedure: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss potato wedges with olive oil, garlic, oregano, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet in a single layer. Roast 35–45 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges. Add lemon slices for the last 10 minutes if desired. Serve hot.
recipes.Notes: For extra crispness, preheat the baking sheet in the oven before adding the potatoes.

recipes.Blurb: A classic Neapolitan garlic-and-oil pasta: simple, aromatic, and perfect with a bubbly.
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
6 oz. (170 g) spaghetti
3–4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
3 tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
¼ tsp. red pepper flakes (or to taste)
Salt, to taste
Fresh parsley, chopped (about 1 tbsp)
Optional: a splash of pasta water to adjust emulsion
recipes.Procedure:
1. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water.
2. In a skillet, heat the olive oil over medium-low. Add the sliced garlic and cook gently until pale gold; do not brown. Add the red pepper flakes and swirl briefly.
3. Add a splash of pasta water to the skillet to begin forming the emulsion.
4. Drain the pasta and add it directly to the skillet. Toss continuously over medium heat until the oil and pasta water emulsify and coat the spaghetti.
5. Season with salt, add the chopped parsley, and toss again. Serve immediately.
recipes.Notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to taste. Fresh parsley should be added at the end for brightness. If the sauce seems dry, add more pasta water a tablespoon at a time until glossy.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
3 cups bread flour
Water to hydrate to 84% (see notes)
¼ cup sourdough starter (do not normalize hydration)
1 tsp. salt
2½ tbsp. sugar
1½ tbsp. dry milk
corn meal
recipes.Procedure:
1. Add starter and water to a bowl, mix well. Add flour, salt, sugar and dry milk. Mix until the liquid is fully incorporated. Turn out on a floured surface and let sit for 1 hour.
2. Perform a set of 4 bowl-folds, one set every 15 minutes, each set consisting of 4 times around the dough. After the fourth set, allow dough to sit 15 minutes more.
3. Perform a set of 5 stretch-and-folds, one set every 30 minutes, each set consisting of 4 steps of stretch, fold in half, rotate dough 90°.
4. Place dough in a grease bowl, cover and allow to rise in a warm place until dough has risen notiecably. Refrigerate overnight.
