5. Divide fermented dough into 15-16 pieces of about 65g each. Place each piece inside a 4" greased muffin ring on parchment which has been sprinkled with corn meal. Sprinkle more corn meal on top of each piece of dough.
6. Oil the bottom of another baking sheet and place over the muffin rings. Allow to rise until ring is filled.
7. Warm a skillet: When ready to cook the muffins, warm a large skillet over medium heat. Melt a small pat of butter — enough to just coat the bottom of the pan and prevent sticking.
8. Cook the muffins 5 to 6 minutes on one side: Working in batches, transfer a few of the muffins to the skillet — allow an inch or so of space between muffins and do not crowd the pan. If using rings, transfer the muffins with their rings to the pan. Cook until the bottoms of the muffins are golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes.
9. Flip and cook 5 to 6 minutes on the other side: Flip the muffins and cook the other side until golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes. If you prefer thinner, less puffy English muffins, you can gently press the tops with the spatula to prevent them from rising too much.
10. Adjust the heat as needed: If your muffins seem to be browning too quickly on the bottoms (or not quickly enough), adjust the heat as needed. (If you find that your muffins are browning too quickly, throw them in the oven at 350°F to finish baking through.)
11. Finish cooking all of the muffins: Transfer cooked muffins to a cooling rack. Continue working in batches until all the muffins have been cooked. Add a small pat of butter to the pan between batches to prevent sticking.
recipes.Notes: Since flour varies, you will need to determine the amount of water to use for your specific flour.  Measure out 3½ cups of bread flour and weigh it, in grams.  Take 84% of that weight: that's the number of ml of water to use.  Measure out that much water for your dough.  You can read off the English measurement from the other side of your measuring cup and note it for future use.

recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
3 lemons or 2 oranges
400 g sugar
400 ml water
sugar (optional)`
recipes.Procedure:
1. Wash fruit. Quarter peel. Trim excess pith. Cut into 6 mm strips.
2. Place peel in pot. Cover with cold water.
3. Bring to boil. Boil 1 minute for lemon peel or 2 minutes for orange peel. Drain.
4. Repeat Step 2–3 more times (total 3 blanches for lemon peel, 4 for orange peel).
5. Combine 400 g. sugar + 400 g. water in pot. Heat until dissolved.
6. Add peel. Simmer on low 45–60 minutes until translucent and flexible. Orange peel requires the lesser time.
7. Remove peel. Spread on rack or parchment. Dry 12–24 hours.
8. Optional: Toss in sugar. Otherwise leave plain.
recipes.Notes: Save the sugar water syrup for cooking: it has a rich, sweet flavor.  Also, if you are making both lemon and orange peel, use the same syrup water for both.

recipes.Blurb: A recipe scaled for a 6" pie pan.
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
3 cups sliced peaches, canned or fresh (about 6 medium peaches)
1 tbsp. lemon juice
½ tsp. lemon zest (optional)
¼ tsp. almond extract (optional)
Pinch of salt
⅓ cup granulated sugar
1–2 tbsp. brown sugar (optional)
2 tbsp. cornstarch OR3 tbsp. flour
1 tbsp. butter, dotted over filling
1  Crust, Standard double crust, scaled for a 6" pie
recipes.Procedure:
1. Toss peaches with sugar, lemon juice, zest, salt, and thickener. Let sit 10 minutes.
2. Fill bottom crust and dot with butter.
3. Add top crust (lattice or vented full crust).
4. Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes.
5. Reduce to 375°F and bake 30–35 minutes more, until juices bubble thickly and crust is golden.
6. Cool at least 3 hours before slicing.

recipes.RecipeName: Chinese-style Broccoli Beef with Peanut-lime Sauce
recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
12 oz. round steak, sliced paper-thin across the grain
1 tsp. soy sauce (for velveting)
1 tsp. cornstarch
1 tsp. neutral oil
1 tbsp. Shaoxing wine or dry sherry (optional)
2 cups broccoli florets (optional but recommended)
1 small onion, thin-sliced (optional)
1/2–3/4 cup Thai peanut–lime sauce
recipes.Procedure:
1. Combine sliced beef with soy sauce, cornstarch, oil, and optional Shaoxing. Mix well and rest 10–15 minutes.
2. Cut broccoli into bite-size florets and slice onion if using.
3. Heat a pan until very hot. Add a splash of oil and stir-fry beef in small batches until just browned. Remove to a plate.
4. Add broccoli and onion to the pan. Stir-fry 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender.
5. Return beef to the pan, reduce heat to low, and add your peanut–lime sauce.
6. Stir gently until everything is coated and warmed through. Do not boil the sauce.

recipes.Blurb: A hearty lasagna built around DFPS, using a 50/50 ricotta and cottage cheese blend for perfect texture.
recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
Dennis' Pasta Sauce, warmed just enough to loosen
Lasagna noodles (boiled or oven-ready)
1 cup Ricotta cheese
1 cup Cottage cheese
1  Egg
2-3 cups Italian blend shredded cheese
Salt and pepper to taste
Optional: basil or parsley
recipes.Procedure:
1. Mix ricotta, cottage cheese, egg, a handful of Italian blend cheese, salt, and pepper until creamy.
2. Warm DFPS slightly so it spreads easily. In a lasagna pan, spread a thin layer of DFPS on the bottom. Add noodles. Add a generous layer of DFPS. Spoon and spread the cheese mixture over the sauce. Sprinkle Italian blend cheese. Add another layer of noodles. Repeat layers until the pan is full. Finish with DFPS and a final layer of shredded cheese. 
3. Cover with foil and bake at 375 degrees for 30–40 minutes.
4. Uncover and bake 10–15 minutes more to brown the top. Let rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.Notes: A 50/50 ricotta and cottage cheese blend gives ideal structure and brightness. DFPS provides all needed seasoning; no additional herbs or garlic required. Lasagna freezes well if prepared in two smaller pans.

recipes.Author: Microsoft Copilot
recipes.Ingredients:
½ pork tenderloin (for two)
Salt and pepper
2 tbsp. Dijon mustard
1 tsp. fresh thyme, chopped
1 tsp. fresh rosemary, chopped
1 clove garlic, minced
1 tbsp. olive oil
¼ cup white wine or chicken stock
1 tbsp. Dijon (for sauce)
1 tbsp. butter
recipes.Procedure:
1. Preheat grill to extreme heat (500–650°F).
2. Pat tenderloin dry; season with salt and pepper only.
3. Sear on grill 2 minutes per side until crust forms.
4. Remove from grill; brush with Dijon, herbs, garlic, olive oil.
5. Return to grill at 350–400°F; cook to 140–145°F internal.
6. Rest under foil 5–10 minutes.
7. Deglaze pan (or small skillet) with wine/stock; whisk in Dijon and butter.
8. Reduce to glossy sauce; slice tenderloin; spoon sauce over.

recipes.Ingredients:
1 pie pumpkin
Sea salt, smoked if desired (optional, if you plan on roasting the seeds).
recipes.Procedure:
1) Halve the pumpkin.
2) Place cut-side down on a parchment-lined sheet.
3) Roast at 375° until it slumps, up to an hour.
4) Let it cool enough to handle. Flip it over and scoop out the seeds and fibers
5) If roasting the seeds, separate them from the cooked fibers, spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet, salt lightly and roast at 325º until golden brown.

recipes.Author: Aaron Scott
recipes.Ingredients:
3½ cups bread flour (100%)
97% water.
1 tsp. salt
1 tsp. dried yeast
recipes.Procedure:
1) Mix all ingredients in a bowl until thoroughly mixed. Dough will be rough-textured. Turn out on a floured work surface and let sit for 1 hour to autolyze.
2) Perform a series of bowl folds, 4 times around the dough. Let dough sit for 15 minutes. Repeat 3 more times.
3) Perform a series of 4 stretch and folds, rotating the dough 90° after each fold. Let dough sit for 30 minutes. Repeat 4 more times.
4) Shape dough into 1 boule, 1 batard or 3 baguettes. Place in a proofing basket lined with parchment and let rise until very puffy.
5) Slash loaf just before baking. Bake in a cloche preheated in the oven at 450º, 30 minutes covered, 8 minutes uncovered.
